value.zh: 於是下恢廷尉，廷尉當恢逗橈，當斬。
value.en: He sent Wang Hui to the commandant of justice, who convicted him of cowardice in the face of the enemy—a capital crime.
value.literal: Thereupon he sent Hui down to the commandant of justice; the commandant of justice judged Hui for dilatory and weak conduct, meriting execution.

value.zh: 恢行千金丞相蚡，蚡不敢言上，而言於太后曰：「王恢首為馬邑事，今不成而硃恢，是為匈奴報仇也。」
value.en: Wang Hui bribed Chancellor Tian Fen with a thousand catties of gold; Tian Fen dared not plead to the emperor but told the empress dowager, "Wang Hui began the Mayi plot; to execute him now is to do the Xiongnu a favor."
value.literal: Hui carried a thousand in gold weight to Chancellor Fen; Fen did not dare speak to the emperor, but spoke to the empress dowager, saying, "Wang Hui was first to propose the Mayi affair; now that it has failed and they would execute Hui, this is to avenge the Xiongnu."

value.zh: 上朝太后，太后以蚡言告上。
value.en: At court with his mother, the emperor heard her repeat Tian Fen's plea.
value.literal: The emperor attended court with the empress dowager; the empress dowager told the emperor Fen's words.

value.zh: 上曰：「首為馬邑事者恢，故發天下兵數十萬，從其言，為此。
value.en: The emperor said, "Wang Hui started Mayi; I mobilized hundreds of thousands on his word.
value.literal: The emperor said, "The one who first proposed the Mayi affair was Hui; therefore I raised several hundred thousand troops of the realm and followed his word in doing this.

value.zh: 且縱單于不可得，恢所部擊，猶頗可得，以尉士大夫心。
value.en: Even if we missed the shanyu, Wang Hui could still have bloodied the baggage train and heartened the army.
value.literal: Moreover even if the shanyu could not be got, what Hui's command struck could still have been largely got—it would have consoled the hearts of gentlemen.

value.zh: 今不誅恢，無以謝天下。」
value.en: If I spare him, I owe the empire an apology."
value.literal: Now if we do not execute Hui, there is no way to apologize to the realm."

value.zh: 於是恢聞，乃自殺。
value.en: Wang Hui killed himself when he heard.
value.literal: Thereupon when Hui heard, he killed himself.

value.zh: 安國為材官將軍，屯漁陽，捕生口虜，言匈奴遠去。
value.en: Han Anguo, as specialist general at Yuyang, took prisoners who swore the Xiongnu had withdrawn deep into the steppe.
value.literal: Anguo was general of specialist troops, encamped at Yuyang, captured living prisoners from the barbarians, who said the Xiongnu had gone far away.

value.zh: 即上言方佃作時，請且罷屯。
value.en: He memorialized that spring planting needed labor and asked to stand the garrison down.
value.literal: He immediately memorialized that it was the season of field work and requested for the nonce to disband the encampment.

value.zh: 罷屯月餘，匈奴大入上谷、漁陽。
value.en: A month after he sent the troops home, the Xiongnu smashed into Shanggu and Yuyang.
value.literal: A month after the encampment was disbanded, the Xiongnu raided in force into Shanggu and Yuyang.

value.zh: 安國壁乃有七百餘人，出與戰，安國傷，入壁。
value.en: Han Anguo had only seven hundred men in his fort; he sortied, was wounded, and crawled back inside.
value.literal: Anguo's rampart then had only more than seven hundred men; he went out to fight; Anguo was wounded and entered the rampart.

value.zh: 匈奴虜略千餘人及畜產去。
value.en: The raiders took over a thousand captives and beasts and rode away.
value.literal: The Xiongnu carried off more than a thousand people and livestock and left.

value.zh: 上怒，使使責讓安國。
value.en: The emperor sent messengers to blister Han Anguo.
value.literal: The emperor was angry and sent envoys to rebuke Anguo.

value.zh: 徙益東，屯右北平。
value.en: He was shifted east to garrison Youbeiping.
value.literal: He was transferred farther east to encamp at Youbeiping.

value.zh: 是時，虜言當入東方。
value.en: Intelligence said the next strike would fall on the eastern sector.
value.literal: At that time the barbarians said they were about to enter the east.

value.zh: 壺遂與太史遷等定漢律歷，官至詹事，其人深中篤行君子。
value.en: Hu Sui worked with Sima Qian and others on the Han calendar and code, rose to chamberlain for the heir apparent, and was remembered as a grave, steady gentleman.
value.literal: Hu Sui, together with Grand Scribe Sima Qian and others, fixed the Han statutes and calendar; he rose to office as chamberlain for the heir apparent; the man was a gentleman of deep moderation and steadfast conduct.

value.zh: 上方倚欲以為相，會其病卒。
value.en: The emperor meant to make him chancellor; he died of illness first.
value.literal: The emperor was leaning on him and wished to make him chancellor, but he fell ill and died.

value.zh: 安國為人多大略，知足以當世取舍，而出於忠厚。
value.en: Han Anguo was broad in strategic vision, wise enough to judge the age's choices, yet fundamentally loyal and honest.
value.literal: Anguo was by nature broad in strategic grasp, his wisdom sufficient for the choices of the age, yet he came from loyalty and honesty.

value.zh: 貪耆財利，然所推舉皆廉士賢於己者。
value.en: He was greedy for wealth, yet everyone he recommended was an upright man more worthy than himself.
value.literal: He was greedy for wealth and profit, yet those he recommended were all upright men more worthy than himself.

value.zh: 於梁舉壺遂、臧固，至它，皆天下名士，士亦以此稱慕之，唯天子以為國器。
value.en: In Liang he recommended Hu Sui and Zang Gu; elsewhere too his picks were famous men of the realm; scholars admired him for it, and the emperor alone treated him as a pillar of state.
value.literal: In Liang he recommended Hu Sui and Zang Gu; everywhere else, all were famous men of the realm; men therefore admired him for this; only the Son of Heaven regarded him as state treasure.

value.zh: 安國為御史大夫五年，丞相蚡薨。
value.en: Han Anguo served five years as censor-in-chief; then Chancellor Tian Fen died.
value.literal: Anguo served as censor-in-chief five years; Chancellor Fen died.

value.zh: 安國行丞相事，引墮車，蹇。
value.en: Han Anguo acted as chancellor; he fell from a carriage while attending to his duties and went lame.
value.literal: Anguo performed chancellor's duties; leading a carriage, he fell from the vehicle and was lame.

value.zh: 上欲用安國為丞相，使使視，蹇甚，乃更以平棘侯薛澤為丞相。
value.en: The emperor meant to make Han Anguo chancellor and sent an envoy to look him over; his limp was too severe, so he appointed Marquis of Pingji Xue Ze instead.
value.literal: The emperor wished to appoint Anguo chancellor and sent an envoy to observe him; his lameness was severe; he then changed to appoint Marquis of Pingji Xue Ze as chancellor.

value.zh: 安國病免，數月，瘉，復為中尉。
value.en: Han Anguo resigned on grounds of illness; months later, recovered, he was reappointed metropolitan commandant.
value.literal: Anguo was dismissed on grounds of illness; after several months he recovered and was again made metropolitan commandant.

value.zh: 歲餘，徙為衛尉。
value.en: A year later he was transferred to chamberlain for the guard.
value.literal: After more than a year he was transferred to be chamberlain for the guard.

value.zh: 而將軍衛青等擊匈奴，破龍城。
value.en: Meanwhile General Wei Qing and others struck the Xiongnu and took Dragon City.
value.literal: Meanwhile General Wei Qing and others attacked the Xiongnu and broke Dragon City.

value.zh: 明年，匈奴大入邊。
value.en: The next year the Xiongnu raided the frontier in force.
value.literal: The next year the Xiongnu raided the border in force.

value.zh: 語在青傳。
value.en: The full account is in the biography of Wei Qing.
value.literal: The account is in Qing's biography.

value.zh: 楊終字子山，蜀郡成都人也。
value.en: Yang Zhong, styled Zishan, came from Chengdu in Shu commandery.
value.literal: Yang Zhong, courtesy name Zishan, was a man of Chengdu in Shu commandery.

value.zh: 年十三，為郡小吏，太守奇其才，遣詣京師受業，習春秋。
value.en: When he was thirteen he served as a junior clerk in the commandery. The grand administrator, struck by his ability, sent him to the capital for schooling, and there he mastered the Spring and Autumn Annals.
value.literal: At age thirteen he became a petty clerk in the commandery; the grand administrator marveled at his talent and sent him to the capital to study, where he learned the Chunqiu.

value.zh: [一]顯宗時，征詣蘭台，拜校書郎。
value.en: Under Emperor Ming he was called to the Orchid Terrace and given the post of collating secretary [1].
value.literal: In the time of Emperor Ming [note 1], he was summoned to the Orchid Terrace and appointed collator.

value.zh: 帝以延儒生，常特宴見。
value.en: Emperor Huan often feasted Yuan Yan alone as a scholar-favorite.
value.literal: Because Yan was a Confucian scholar, the emperor often gave him special feasts and audiences.

value.zh: 時太史令上言客星經帝坐，帝密以問延。
value.en: When a stray star crossed the throne asterism, the emperor quietly asked Yuan Yan what it meant.
value.literal: At that time the grand astrologer submitted that a guest star had crossed the emperor's seat; the emperor secretly asked Yan about it.

value.zh: 延因上封事曰：「臣聞天子尊無為上，故天以為子，位臨臣庶，威重四海。
value.en: Yan thereupon submitted a sealed memorial, saying: 'I have heard the Son of Heaven is honored as none above—therefore Heaven makes him son; his position overlooks ministers and commoners; his awesome might fills the four seas.
value.literal: Yan thereupon submitted a sealed memorial, saying: 'I have heard the Son of Heaven is honored as none above—therefore Heaven makes him son; his position overlooks ministers and commoners; his awesome might fills the four seas.

value.zh: 動靜以禮，則星辰順序；
value.en: Right conduct keeps the constellations in harmony;
value.literal: When movement and stillness follow ritual, then the stars march in order;

value.zh: 意有邪僻，則晷度錯違。
value.en: wicked intent throws the calendar and omens out of true.
value.literal: if the mind harbors depravity, then the gnomon's degrees miss and violate.

value.zh: 陛下以河南尹鄧萬有龍潛之舊，封為通侯，恩重公卿，惠豐宗室。
value.en: Emperor Huan ennobled Deng Wan, an old companion from before the throne, beyond normal ministerial favor.
value.literal: Your Majesty, because metropolitan governor of Henan Deng Wan had old ties from before your accession, enfeoffed him as full marquis—favor heavier than the dukes and ministers, bounty rich for the imperial house.

value.zh: 加頃引見，與之對博，上下媟黷，有虧尊嚴。
value.en: He added that gambling with Wan in public shamed the throne.
value.literal: Further you lately summoned him to meet and played liubo with him; high and low were lewd and defiled, injuring august dignity.

value.zh: 臣聞之，帝左右者，所以咨政德也。
value.en: Court companions should refine policy, not dice games.
value.literal: Your servant has heard that those at the emperor's left and right are the means to consult on virtue in government.

value.zh: 故周公戒成王曰『其朋其朋』，言慎所與也。
value.en: He quoted the Documents' warning about friends of the ruler.
value.literal: Therefore the Duke of Zhou warned King Cheng, saying 'Be careful of your companions, be careful of your companions'—meaning be careful whom you befriend.

value.zh: [一]昔宋閔公與強臣共博，列婦人於側，積此無禮，以致大災。
value.en: [1] Duke Min of Song's fatal dice game illustrated the danger.
value.literal: [1] Formerly Duke Min of Song played liubo with a powerful minister, ranged women at the side—accumulating such lack of ritual led to great disaster.

value.zh: [二]武帝與幸臣李延年﹑韓嫣同臥起，尊爵重賜，情慾無猒，遂生驕淫之心，行不義之事，卒延年被戮，嫣伏其辜。
value.en: [2] Emperor Wu's intimacy with singers ended in executions.
value.literal: [2] Emperor Wu slept and rose with favored ministers Li Yannian and Han Yan, honored them with noble rank and heavy gifts, lust and appetite insatiable—thereupon arose arrogant and dissolute hearts, unrighteous deeds were done, and in the end Yannian was executed and Yan submitted to his crime.

value.zh: [三]夫愛之則不覺其過，惡之則不知其善，所以事多放濫，物情生怨。
value.en: [3] Passion blinds rulers to fault and merit alike.
value.literal: [3] When you love them you do not notice their faults; when you hate them you do not know their good—therefore affairs mostly run wild and feeling breeds resentment.

value.zh: 注[三]李延年，中山人也。
value.en: Commentary [3]: Li Yannian's origin.
value.literal: Note [3] Li Yannian was a man of Zhongshan.

value.zh: 身及父母兄弟皆故倡人也。
value.en: His whole family were performers.
value.literal: He and his parents and brothers had all been entertainers.

value.zh: 武帝時，延年女弟得幸，號曰李夫人。
value.en: His sister became Lady Li.
value.literal: In Emperor Wu's time his younger sister won favor—she was titled Lady Li.

value.zh: 延年善歌舞，為協律都尉，佩二千石印綬，與上臥起。
value.en: He rose to music director with ministerial rank and shared the emperor's bed.
value.literal: Yannian was skilled at songs and dances, became director of harmony, wore a two-thousand-bushel seal ribbon, and slept and rose with the emperor.

value.zh: 弟季與中人亂，出入驕恣，上遂誅延年兄弟。
value.en: His brother's scandal cost the whole family their lives.
value.literal: His younger brother Ji debauched with a palace man, came and went arrogantly; the emperor thereupon executed Yannian and his brothers.

value.zh: 韓嫣，韓王信之曾孫也。
value.en: Han Yan descended from Han Xin.
value.literal: Han Yan was the great-grandson of King Xin of Han.

value.zh: 武帝為王時，與嫣相愛，後位至上大夫，賞賜擬鄧通，與上臥起，出入永巷，以奸聞被誅。
value.en: Yan had been Wu's boyhood favorite until scandal brought execution.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu was a king he loved Yan; later his rank reached senior grandee; rewards rivaled Deng Tong's; he slept and rose with the emperor, went in and out of the long lanes, and was executed when his debauchery was heard.

value.zh: 後漢書志第二 律歷中 賈逵論歷永元論歷延光論歷漢安論歷熹平論歷論月食
value.en: Treatise Two of the Book of Later Han: Music and Calendars, Part Two — Treatises on Jia Kui's calendar memorials and the debates under Yongyuan, Yanguang, Han'an, and Xiping, together with the discussion of lunar eclipses
value.literal: Book of Later Han, Treatise Two: Pitch-Pipes and Calendar, Part Two — On Jia Kui Discussing the Calendar, On the Yongyuan Discussion of the Calendar, On the Yanguang Discussion of the Calendar, On the Han'an Discussion of the Calendar, On the Xiping Discussion of the Calendar, On Lunar Eclipses

value.zh: 愍懷太子
value.en: Crown Prince Minhuai
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai

value.zh: 湣懷太子遹，字熙祖，惠帝長子，母曰謝才人。
value.en: Sima Yu, styled Xizu, was Emperor Hui's firstborn—his mother was Lady Xie of Talented rank.
value.literal: Crown Prince Minhuai, Yu, courtesy name Xizu, was Emperor Hui's eldest son; his mother was Talented Lady Xie.

value.zh: 幼而聰慧，武帝愛之，恆在左右。
value.en: Wu Di doted on the bright boy and kept him always near.
value.literal: From childhood he was clever and bright; Emperor Wu loved him and kept him always at his side.

value.zh: 嘗與諸皇子共戲殿上，惠帝來朝，執諸皇子手，次至太子，帝曰：「是汝兒也。」
value.en: Once he was playing on the palace steps with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience, he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, the emperor said, 'This is your son.'
value.literal: Once he was playing on the palace steps with the imperial princes; when Emperor Hui came to audience he took each prince's hand in turn; when he reached the crown prince, Emperor Wu said, 'This is your son.'

value.zh: 惠帝乃止。
value.en: Hui broke off his greeting.
value.literal: Emperor Hui thereupon stopped.

value.zh: 宮中嘗夜失火，武帝登樓望之。
value.en: A night blaze drew Wu Di to a high gallery.
value.literal: Once at night the palace caught fire; Emperor Wu climbed a tower to watch.

value.zh: 太子時年五歲，牽帝裾入暗中。
value.en: Five-year-old Yu pulled his grandfather into the dark.
value.literal: The crown prince was then five years old; he tugged the emperor's robe into the shadows.

value.zh: 帝問其故，太子曰：「暮夜倉卒，宜備非常，不宜令照見人君也。」
value.en: The crown prince said, "Suddenly at night one must guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face."
value.literal: The emperor asked why; the crown prince said, 'Suddenly at night one should guard against the unexpected; one must not let firelight reveal the ruler's face.'

value.zh: 由是奇之。
value.en: Wu Di marked him extraordinary.
value.literal: From this Wu Di marveled at him.

value.zh: 嘗從帝觀豕牢，言於帝曰：「豕甚肥，何不殺以享士，而使久費五穀？」
value.en: While watching the imperial sty he said to the emperor, "The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?"
value.literal: Once when following the emperor to view the pig pen he said to the emperor, 'The pigs are very fat—why not slaughter them to feast the troops instead of letting them waste grain forever?'

value.zh: 帝嘉其意，即使烹之。
value.en: Wu Di approved and had them slaughtered.
value.literal: The emperor praised his intent and at once ordered them cooked.

value.zh: 因撫其背，謂廷尉傅祗曰：「此兒當興我家。」
value.en: He stroked the boy's back and told Court Commandant Fu Zhi, "This child will bring prosperity to our house."
value.literal: He therefore stroked the boy's back and said to Court Commandant Fu Zhi, 'This child will bring prosperity to our house.'

value.zh: 嘗對群臣稱太子似宣帝，於是令譽流於天下。
value.en: He likened the heir to Sima Yi before court—reputation followed.
value.literal: He once declared before the assembled ministers that the crown prince resembled Emperor Xuan; thereafter praise of him spread through the realm.

value.zh: 及賈庶人死，乃誅劉振、孫慮、程據等，冊復太子曰：「皇帝使使持節、兼司空、衛尉伊策故皇太子之靈曰：嗚呼！
value.en: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: "The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!
value.literal: When Deposed Commoner Jia died, they executed Liu Zhen, Sun Lü, Cheng Ju, and others, and posthumously restored the crown prince; the edict read: 'The emperor dispatches the credential-bearer, concurrent Director of Works, Commandant of the Guard Yi to announce by patent to the spirit of the late crown prince: Alas!

value.zh: 維爾少資岐嶷之質，荷先帝殊異之寵，大啟土宇，奄有淮陵。
value.en: In youth you were endowed with precocious wisdom and enjoyed the late emperor’s exceptional affection. He granted you a great domain and possession of Huailing.
value.literal: In youth you were endowed with precocious wisdom and enjoyed the late emperor’s exceptional affection. He granted you a great domain and possession of Huailing.

value.zh: 朕奉遵遺旨，越建爾儲副，以光顯我祖宗。
value.en: I followed his last wishes and established you as heir, to glorify our ancestors.
value.literal: I followed his last wishes and established you as heir, to glorify our ancestors.

value.zh: 祗爾德行，以從保傅，事親孝敬，禮無違者。
value.en: You were to revere virtuous conduct and follow your tutors, serve your parents with filial respect, and never violate ritual.
value.literal: I charged you to follow tutors in virtue, serving parents with filial respect—ritual unbreached.

value.zh: 而朕昧於凶構，致爾於非命之禍，俾申生、孝己復見於今。
value.en: Yet I failed to perceive wicked intrigues and brought you to an unnatural death, so that Shen Sheng and Xiao Ji appeared again in our time.
value.literal: Yet I, dim to vicious plots, brought you to the misfortune of untimely death, making Shen Sheng and Xiao Ji again appear in our day.

value.zh: 賴宰相賢明，人神憤怨，用啟朕心，討厥有罪，咸伏其辜。
value.en: Fortunately, wise ministers and the indignation of men and spirits opened my eyes; I punished the guilty, and all paid the penalty for their crimes.
value.literal: Thanks to wise ministers, human and spirit alike resented, opening my heart to punish the guilty—each has met sentence.

value.zh: 何補於荼毒冤魂酷痛哉？
value.en: But how can that make amends for the cruel suffering inflicted upon your wronged spirit?
value.literal: What use mending poisoned wronged souls' cruel pain?

value.zh: 是用忉怛悼恨，震動於五內。
value.en: Thus I grieve in anguish and regret, shaken to my innermost being.
value.literal: Therefore grief tears my vitals and shakes my five inner organs.

value.zh: 今追復皇太子喪禮，反葬京畿，祠乙太牢。
value.en: Now I restore the funeral rites due the crown prince, return your burial to the capital region, and offer a full tailao sacrifice of ox, sheep, and pig.
value.literal: Now I restore the funeral rites due the crown prince, return your burial to the capital region, and offer a full tailao sacrifice of ox, sheep, and pig.

value.zh: 魂而有靈，尚獲爾心。」
value.en: If soul possesses awareness may it receive this heart."
value.literal: If soul possesses awareness may it receive this heart.'

value.zh: 帝為太子服長子斬衰，群臣齊衰，使尚書和郁率東宮官屬具吉凶之制，迎太子喪于許昌。
value.en: Court mourned and fetched Yu's bier from Xu.
value.literal: The emperor wore unhemmed mourning for the crown prince as for an eldest son; the ministers wore hemmed mourning. He sent Minister He Yu to lead the Eastern Palace officials in preparing the prescribed auspicious and mourning rites and bringing the crown prince's bier back from Xuchang.

value.zh: 喪之發也，大風雷電，幃蓋飛裂。
value.en: Storm shattered funeral umbrellas.
value.literal: When the hearse set out great wind and thunder came—canopies and coverings flew torn.

value.zh: 又為哀策曰：「皇帝臨軒，使洗馬劉務告于皇太子之殯曰：咨爾遹！
value.en: They further composed a condolence text: "The emperor facing the gallery sends Groom of the Household Liu Wu to the crown prince's lying-in-state: Ah, Yu!
value.literal: They further composed a condolence text: 'The emperor facing the gallery sends Groom of the Household Liu Wu to the crown prince's lying-in-state: Ah, Yu!

value.zh: 幼稟英挺，芬馨誕茂。
value.en: From childhood you were outstanding, and your fine qualities flourished abundantly.
value.literal: You drew from youth heroic sap, fragrance ripe at birth.

value.zh: 既表髫齔，高明逸秀。
value.en: Even in early boyhood you displayed lofty brilliance and exceptional talents.
value.literal: Already in tied hair you stood lofty and bright.

value.zh: 昔爾聖祖，嘉爾淑美。
value.en: Your august grandfather cherished your fine virtues.
value.literal: Your holy ancestor prized your fine virtue.

value.zh: 顯詔仍崇，名振同軌。
value.en: Illustrious edicts repeatedly increased your honors; your fame resounded throughout the realm.
value.literal: Illustrious edicts repeatedly increased your honors; your fame resounded throughout the realm.

value.zh: 是用建爾儲副，永統皇基。
value.en: Therefore I established you as heir, to perpetuate the imperial foundations forever.
value.literal: Therefore I established you as heir, to perpetuate the imperial foundations forever.

value.zh: 如何凶戾潛構，禍害如茲！
value.en: How did vicious cruelty secretly weave harm like this!
value.literal: How did vicious cruelty secretly weave harm like this!

value.zh: 哀感和氣，痛貫四時。
value.en: Sorrow moves harmonious qi; pain pierces four seasons.
value.literal: Sorrow moves harmonious qi; pain pierces four seasons.

value.zh: 嗚呼哀哉！
value.en: Alas, how grievous!
value.literal: Alas, alas the sorrow!

value.zh: 爾之降廢，實我不明。
value.en: Your degradation was truly due to my lack of discernment.
value.literal: Your degradation was truly my blindness.

value.zh: 牝亂沈烖，釁結禍成。
value.en: A woman’s disorder brought deep calamity; hostility accumulated and disaster took shape.
value.literal: Female chaos sank calamity; omens knotted into disaster.

value.zh: 爾之逝矣，誰百其形？
value.en: Now that you have departed, who could offer a hundredfold ransom for your person?
value.literal: Now that you have departed, who could offer a hundredfold ransom for your person?

value.zh: 昔之申生，含枉莫訟。
value.en: Long ago Shen Sheng bore false charges, with none to plead his case.
value.literal: Long ago Shen Sheng bore wrong yet could not plead.

value.zh: 今爾之負，抱冤於東。
value.en: Now you too bear unjust blame and nurse your grievance in the east.
value.literal: Now your burden of grievance hugs the eastern lands.

value.zh: 悠悠有識，孰不哀慟！
value.en: Among all who understand, who would not grieve?
value.literal: Far and near anyone with insight—who fails bitter grief!

value.zh: 壺關幹主，千秋悟己。
value.en: The elder of Huguan remonstrated with his ruler; Qianqiu brought him to recognize his error.
value.literal: The elder of Huguan remonstrated with his ruler; Qianqiu brought him to recognize his error.

value.zh: 異世同規，古今一理。
value.en: Across different ages, the pattern is the same; past and present share one principle.
value.literal: Different age, same rule—past and present one principle.

value.zh: 皇孫啟建，隆祚爾子。
value.en: Your son has been established as imperial grandson-heir, continuing the dynastic blessing through him.
value.literal: Your son has been established as imperial grandson-heir, continuing the dynastic blessing through him.

value.zh: 雖悴前終，庶榮後始。
value.en: Though your own end was sorrowful, may the new beginning afterward be glorious.
value.literal: Though front end withered, rear blossom may yet flourish.

value.zh: 窀穸既營，將寧爾神。
value.en: Your burial chamber is now prepared, to bring your spirit peace.
value.literal: Burial vault now built—we pacify your spirit.

value.zh: 華髦電逝，戎車雷震。
value.en: Splendid plumes flash past like lightning; war chariots rumble like thunder.
value.literal: Flower feathers flash like lightning; war wagons thunder.

value.zh: 芒芒羽蓋，翼翼縉紳。
value.en: Feathered canopies stretch far and wide; the gentry advance in orderly ranks.
value.literal: Vast feather-canopies; crowded sash-and-hat ranks.

value.zh: 同悲等痛，孰不酸辛！
value.en: Courtiers weep together.
value.literal: Shared grief and equal pain—who lacks bitter sorrow!

value.zh: 庶光來葉，永世不泯。」
value.en: May light reach posterity, never extinguished through ages."
value.literal: May light reach posterity, never extinguished through ages.'

value.zh: 諡曰湣懷。
value.en: Canonized Crown Prince Minhuai.
value.literal: Posthumous title Minhuai was granted.

value.zh: 六月己卯，葬于顯平陵。
value.en: Buried sixth month at Xianping.
value.literal: On jimao day of the sixth month he was buried at Xianping Mausoleum.

value.zh: 帝感閻纘之言，立思子台，故臣江統、陸機並作誄頌焉。
value.en: Yan Zuan's plea built Son-Lament Terrace—Jiang Tong and Lu Ji wrote elegies.
value.literal: Moved by Yan Zuan's words the emperor raised a Terrace of Longing for Sons; former ministers Jiang Tong and Lu Ji both composed dirges.

value.zh: 太子三子：虨、臧、尚，並與父同幽金墉。
value.en: Three sons shared Yu's prison.
value.literal: The crown prince had three sons—Bin, Zang, and Shang—all imprisoned with their father at Jinyong.

value.zh: 史臣曰：湣懷挺岐嶷之姿，表夙成之質。
value.en: The historiographers say: Minhuai was endowed with exceptional wisdom and displayed precocious gifts.
value.literal: The historiographers say: Minhuai bore a posture keen and wise, displaying precocious substance.

value.zh: 武皇鍾愛，既深詒厥之謀；
value.en: Wu Di planned Yu as future pillar.
value.literal: Emperor Wu cherished him and deeply laid succession plans.

value.zh: 天下歸心，頗有後來之望。
value.en: The realm expected greatness.
value.literal: All under Heaven turned hearts toward him—high hopes attended his future.

value.zh: 及於繼明宸極，守器春坊，四教不勤，三朝或闕，豹姿未變，鳳德已衰，信惑奸邪，疏斥正士，好屠酤之賤役，耽苑囿之佚遊，可謂靡不有初，鮮克有終者也。
value.en: When the new ruler ascended the imperial throne and the prince guarded the succession in the Eastern Palace, he neglected the four teachings and sometimes omitted the three daily greetings. His leopard’s form was not yet transformed, while his phoenix virtue had already declined. He trusted wicked deceivers and drove away upright men, enjoyed the lowly work of butchering and selling wine, and indulged in idle outings in the parks. Truly one may say: "All have a beginning, but few carry through to the end."
value.literal: When the new ruler ascended the imperial throne and the prince guarded the succession in the Eastern Palace, he neglected the four teachings and sometimes omitted the three daily greetings. His leopard’s form was not yet transformed, while his phoenix virtue had already declined. He trusted wicked deceivers and drove away upright men, enjoyed the lowly work of butchering and selling wine, and indulged in idle outings in the parks. Truly one may say: "All have a beginning, but few carry through to the end."

value.zh: 既而中宮凶忍，久懷危害之心，外戚諂諛，競進讒邪之說；
value.en: Thereupon the inner palace proved fierce and cruel, long harboring murderous intent; outer kin flattered, competing to advance slander.
value.literal: Thereupon the inner palace proved fierce and cruel, long harboring murderous intent; outer kin flattered, competing to advance slander.

value.zh: 坎牲之謀已構，斃犬之譖遂行；
value.en: The plot involving a sacrificial victim had already been laid; the slander involving a dead dog then took effect.
value.literal: The plot involving a sacrificial victim had already been laid; the slander involving a dead dog then took effect.

value.zh: 一人乏探隱之聰，百辟無爭臣之節。
value.en: The ruler lacked the discernment to uncover hidden matters, and the ministers lacked the integrity to remonstrate.
value.literal: Thus one man lacked keen insight into hidden matters; the hundred ministers showed no temper of remonstrating subjects.

value.zh: 遂使冤逾楚建，酷甚戾園。
value.en: Thus the injustice exceeded that done to Jian of Chu, and the cruelty surpassed the tragedy commemorated at Li Garden.
value.literal: Thus the injustice exceeded that done to Jian of Chu, and the cruelty surpassed the tragedy commemorated at Li Garden.

value.zh: 雖復禮備哀榮，情深憫慟，亦何補於荼毒者哉！
value.en: Posthumous honors could not resurrect him.
value.literal: Though mourning rites ran full and grief ran deep, what did they mend for the poisoned innocent!

value.zh: 贊曰：湣懷聰穎，諒惟天挺。
value.en: The encomium says: Minhuai was intelligent and perceptive, truly endowed by Heaven.
value.literal: The encomium says: Minhuai clever and keen—truly Heaven-endowed.

value.zh: 皇祖鐘心，庶僚引領。
value.en: His imperial grandfather cherished him deeply; the assembled officials looked forward in expectation.
value.literal: Imperial ancestor pinned hope on him; hosts of officials craned necks.

value.zh: 震宮肇建，儲德不恢。
value.en: When he first entered the heir’s palace, his princely virtue failed to grow.
value.literal: When Thunder Palace first rose, heir virtue never broadened.

value.zh: 掇蜂構隙，歸胙生災。
value.en: Gathering wasps opened a breach; sending back sacrificial meat brought disaster.
value.literal: Gathering wasps opened a breach; sending back sacrificial meat brought disaster.

value.zh: 既罹凶忍，徒望歸來。
value.en: Death ended every hope of restoration.
value.literal: Once brutal cruelty struck, vain hope alone remained of return.

value.zh: 唐禮：四時各以孟月享太廟，每室用太牢，季冬蠟祭之後，以辰日臘享於太廟，用牲如時祭。
value.en: Tang ritual: each season's first month, offerings at the Great Temple—tai lao per chamber. After twelfth-month wax and la, a chen-day la feast at the temple used seasonal victims.
value.literal: Tang rites: In each of the four seasons, in the first month of the season, offerings were made to the Great Ancestral Temple; for each chamber the great offering was used. After the wax sacrifices following the twelfth month's la rites, on a chen day a la offering was presented at the Great Temple, with victims as at the seasonal sacrifices.

value.zh: 三年一祫，以孟冬。
value.en: A he rite every three years, in mid-winter's opening month.
value.literal: Every three years a he sacrifice, in the first month of winter.

value.zh: 五年一禘，以孟夏。
value.en: A di rite every five years, in mid-summer's opening month.
value.literal: Every five years a di sacrifice, in the first month of summer.

value.zh: 又時享之日，修七祀於太廟西門內之道南：司命，戶以春，灶以夏；
value.en: On seasonal offering days the Seven Sacrifices were kept on the lane south of the temple's west gate—Spirit of Fate; Household Spirit in spring, Stove Spirit in summer;
value.literal: On days of seasonal offerings, the Seven Sacrifices were maintained on the road south within the western gate of the Great Temple: Spirit of Fate; the Household Spirit in spring, the Stove Spirit in summer;

value.zh: 門，厲以秋，行以冬，中溜則于季夏迎氣日祀之。
value.en: Gate and Pestilence Spirits in autumn, Road Spirit in winter; Central Gutter on the last-summer qi-reception day.
value.literal: the Gate Spirit and the Pestilence Spirit in autumn, the Road Spirit in winter; the Central Gutter was sacrificed on the day of receiving seasonal qi in the last month of summer.

value.zh: 若品物時新堪進御者，所司先送太常，與尚食相知，簡擇精好者，以滋味與新物相宜者配之。
value.en: Seasonal delicacies fit for the throne went first to the Court of Sacrifices and the Provisioners, who picked the best and matched flavor to the new offering.
value.literal: If seasonal novelties were fit to present to the sovereign, the responsible office first sent them to the Court of Imperial Sacrifices and coordinated with the Imperial Provisioners, selecting the finest and pairing them with flavors suited to the new goods.

value.zh: 太常卿奉薦於太廟，不出神主。
value.en: The Minister of Sacrifices presented at the Great Temple without removing the tablets.
value.literal: The Minister of Imperial Sacrifices presented offerings at the Great Temple without bringing out the spirit tablets.

value.zh: 仲春薦冰，亦如之。
value.en: Mid-spring ice offerings followed the same rule.
value.literal: In mid-spring ice was presented—in the same manner.

value.zh: 時太常卿姜皎復與禮官上表曰：「臣聞敬宗尊祖，享德崇恩，必也正名，用光時憲，禮也。
value.en: Director Jiang Jiao and the ritual officials again memorialized: "We hear that revering ancestors and exalting grace require correct titles to honor the age's laws—that is ritual.
value.literal: At that time Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices Jiang Jiao again, with ritual officials, submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant has heard that revering the clan and honoring ancestors, enjoying virtue and exalting grace, must rectify names to illuminate the statutes of the age—this is ritual.

value.zh: 伏見太廟中則天皇后配高宗天皇大帝，題云『天后聖帝武氏』。
value.en: In the Grand Temple Empress Zetian shares sacrifice with Emperor Gaozong, inscribed as "Holy Emperor Wu of the Heavenly Empress."
value.literal: We note in the Grand Temple Empress Zetian is enshrined with Emperor Gaozong Tianhuang Dadi, the inscription reading "Holy Emperor Wu of the Heavenly Empress."

value.zh: 伏尋昔居寵秩，親承顧托，因攝大政，事乃從權。
value.en: She once held favored rank, received the late emperor's trust, and took power as an expedient measure.
value.literal: We trace how in the past she held favored rank and personally received the entrustment; she then assumed great government, the affair being one of expedient power.

value.zh: 神龍之初，已去帝號。
value.en: At the start of Shenlong her imperial title had already been removed.
value.literal: At the beginning of Shenlong the imperial title was already removed.

value.zh: 岑羲等不閑政體，復題帝名。
value.en: Cen Xi and others, ignorant of governance, restored an imperial title on the inscription.
value.literal: Cen Xi and others were unversed in the body of government and again inscribed an imperial name.

value.zh: 若又使帝號長存，恐非聖朝通典。
value.en: To let an imperial title stand again would violate court precedent.
value.literal: If the imperial title is again made to endure long, I fear it is not the general statute of the sagely court.

value.zh: 夫七廟者，高祖神堯皇帝之廟也。
value.en: The seven temples are those of the High Ancestor, Emperor Shen Yao.
value.literal: The seven temples are the temples of the High Ancestor, the Divine Yao Emperor.

value.zh: 父昭子穆，祖德宗功，非夫帝子天孫，乘乾出震者，不得升祔於斯矣。
value.en: Father-zhao, son-mu, ancestral merit—only imperial sons and heaven's grandsons who received the mandate may be enshrined there.
value.literal: Father zhao, son mu; ancestral virtue and clan achievement—none but sons of emperors and grandsons of Heaven, those who mount Qian and issue from Zhen, may ascend to enshrinement there.

value.zh: 但皇后祔廟，配食高宗，位號舊章，無宜稱帝。
value.en: Yet as consort sharing Gaozong's sacrifices, her old titles should not include "emperor.
value.literal: But the empress enshrined in the temple, sharing sacrifice with Gaozong, by old title and statute ought not be called emperor.

value.zh: 今山陵日近，陞祔非遙，請申陳告之儀，因除『聖帝』之字，直題云『則天皇后武氏』。」
value.en: With her enshrinement near, we ask to perform the announcement rite, drop "Holy Emperor," and inscribe only "Empress Zetian Wu."
value.literal: Now the imperial tomb day draws near and ascent to enshrinement is not distant; we ask to declare the announcement rite and remove the words "Holy Emperor," inscribing simply "Empress Zetian Wu."

value.zh: 詔從之。
value.en: The emperor approved.
value.literal: The edict followed it.

value.zh: 時既另造義宗廟，將作大匠韋湊上疏曰：「臣聞王者制體，是曰規模；
value.en: A separate Yizong Temple had been built; Master of Works Wei Cou wrote: "A king's institutions are his model;
value.literal: At that time a separate Yizong Temple had been built; Master of Works Wei Cou submitted a memorial, saying: "Your servant has heard that the king establishes the body—this is called the model;

value.zh: 規模之興，實資師古；
value.en: and models must learn from antiquity;
value.literal: the rise of the model in fact relies on taking antiquity as teacher;

value.zh: 師古之道，必也正名；
value.en: which requires correct names;
value.literal: the Way of taking antiquity as teacher must rectify names;

value.zh: 惟名與實，固當相副。
value.en: name and fact must agree.
value.literal: names and reality solidly ought to match each other.

value.zh: 其在宗廟，禮之大者，豈可失哉！
value.en: In the ancestral temple, the greatest rite—how can it be neglected!
value.literal: As for the ancestral temple, the greatest of rites—how can it be lost!

value.zh: 禮，祖有功而宗有德。
value.en: Ritual holds that ancestors have merit and clan lords have virtue.
value.literal: Ritual: the ancestor has merit, the clan lord has virtue.

value.zh: 祖宗之廟，百代不毀。
value.en: Ancestor and clan-lord temples stand for a hundred generations.
value.literal: The temples of ancestor and clan lord are not destroyed for a hundred generations.

value.zh: 故殷太甲曰太宗，太戊曰中宗，武丁曰高宗。
value.en: Yin's Tai Jia was styled Taizong, Tai Wu Zhongzong, and Wu Ding Gaozong.
value.literal: Thus Yin's Tai Jia was called Taizong, Tai Wu Zhongzong, Wu Ding Gaozong.

value.zh: 周宗文王、武王。
value.en: Zhou honored Kings Wen and Wu.
value.literal: Zhou honored King Wen and King Wu.

value.zh: 漢則文帝為太宗，武帝為世宗。
value.en: Han styled Emperor Wen Taizong and Emperor Wu Shizong.
value.literal: Han made Emperor Wen Taizong and Emperor Wu Shizong.

value.zh: 其後代有稱宗，皆以方制海內，德澤可宗，列于昭穆，期於不毀。
value.en: Later rulers styled "zong" when their virtue filled the realm and merited lasting place in the zhao-mu sequence.
value.literal: Afterward generations had those styled "zong," all because they regulated the realm within the four seas and their virtue and grace could be honored; ranked in zhao and mu, they were expected not to be destroyed.

value.zh: 祖宗之義，不亦大乎！
value.en: The weight of "ancestor" and "zong" is immense!
value.literal: Is the meaning of "ancestor" and "zong" not also great!

value.zh: 況孝敬皇帝位止東宮，未嘗南面，聖道誠冠于儲副，德教不被於寰瀛，立廟稱宗，恐非合體。
value.en: Emperor Xiaojing never ruled; though his virtue surpassed other heirs, his teaching did not reach the realm—calling him "zong" does not fit ritual.
value.literal: Moreover Emperor Xiaojing's position stopped at the Eastern Palace; he never faced south. His sagely Way indeed topped the heir, yet his moral teaching did not spread through the realm—establishing a temple and styling him zong, I fear, is not fitting the body of ritual.

value.zh: 況別起寢廟，不入昭穆，稽諸祀典，何義稱宗？
value.en: A separate shrine outside the zhao-mu line: how can it be called "zong" under the sacrifice canon?
value.literal: Moreover, if a separate sleeping temple is erected and he does not enter the zhao-mu sequence, then when this is checked against the sacrifice canon, by what principle can he be called zong?

value.zh: 而廟號義宗，稱之萬代。
value.en: Yet the temple name Yizong would stand for ages.
value.literal: Yet the temple name Yizong would be spoken for ten thousand generations.

value.zh: 以臣庸識，竊謂不可。
value.en: In my humble view it should not be done.
value.literal: By your servant's shallow knowledge, I privately deem it impossible.

value.zh: 望更令有司詳定，務合於禮。」
value.en: I hope you will further order the relevant offices to examine in detail and ensure conformity with ritual."
value.literal: I hope you will further order the relevant offices to examine in detail and ensure conformity with ritual."

value.zh: 於是太常請以本諡「孝敬」為廟稱。
value.en: The Court of Imperial Sacrifices then proposed "Xiaojing," his posthumous title, as the temple name.
value.literal: Thereupon the Court of Imperial Sacrifices requested using the original posthumous title "Xiaojing" as the temple name.

value.zh: 從之。
value.en: Approved.
value.literal: It was approved.

value.zh: 褚遂良 韓瑗 來濟 上官儀
value.en: Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, Lai Ji, and Shang Guanyi
value.literal: Chu Suiliang, Han Yuan, Lai Ji, Shang Guanyi

value.zh: 臣聞古者哲後，必先事華夏而後夷狄，務廣德化，不事遐荒。
value.en: I have heard that in antiquity wise rulers first attended to the Hua-Xia and afterward to the Yi-Di, striving to extend virtue and transformation rather than serving distant wilds.
value.literal: This subject has heard that in antiquity wise rulers first attended to the Hua-Xia and afterward to the Yi-Di, striving to extend virtue and transformation, not serving distant wilds.

value.zh: 是以周宣薄伐，至境而止；
value.en: Therefore King Xuan of Zhou made a light campaign, reaching the border and stopping;
value.literal: Therefore King Xuan of Zhou made a light campaign, reaching the border and stopping;

value.zh: 始皇遠塞，中國分離。
value.en: the First Emperor made distant barriers, and China was divided.
value.literal: the First Emperor made distant barriers, and China was divided.

value.zh: 漢武負文、景之聚財，玩士馬之餘力，始通西域，初置校尉。
value.en: Emperor Wu of Han relied on the accumulated wealth of Emperors Wen and Jing and played with the remaining strength of soldiers and horses. He first opened the Western Regions and first established commandants.
value.literal: Emperor Wu of Han relied on Wen and Jing's accumulated wealth, played with remaining strength of soldiers and horses, first opened the Western Regions, first established commandants.

value.zh: 軍旅連出，將三十年。
value.en: Armies went forth in succession for nearly thirty years.
value.literal: Armies and brigades went forth in succession for nearly thirty years.

value.zh: 復得天馬於宛城，采蒲萄於安息。
value.en: He obtained heavenly horses at Wancheng and gathered grapes at Parthia.
value.literal: He again obtained heavenly horses at Wancheng and gathered grapes at Parthia.

value.zh: 而海內虛竭，生人失所，租及六畜，算至舟車，因之凶年，盜賊並起，搜粟都尉桑弘羊復希主意，遣士卒遠田輪台，築城以威西域。
value.en: Yet the realm was emptied and exhausted, the living lost their homes, levies reached even the six livestock, and assessments reached boats and chariots. Because of this there were famine years and bandits rose together. Search-for-Grain Commandant Sang Hongyang again hoped for the ruler's intent and sent soldiers to farm Luntai from afar and build walls to awe the Western Regions.
value.literal: Yet within the seas was emptied and exhausted, living people lost their places, levies reaching the six livestock, assessments reaching boats and chariots—because of this there were famine years, bandits and robbers rose together; Search-for-Grain Commandant Sang Hongyang again hoped for the ruler's intent, sent soldiers to farm Luntai from afar, built walls to awe the Western Regions.

value.zh: 帝翻然追悔，情發於中，棄輪台之野，下哀痛之詔，人神感悅，海內乃康。
value.en: The emperor suddenly turned and regretted, feeling arising from within. He abandoned the fields of Luntai and issued the edict of mournful pain. Men and spirits were moved and pleased, and the realm then knew peace.
value.literal: The Emperor suddenly turned and regretted, feeling arising from within, abandoned the fields of Luntai, issued the edict of mournful pain—men and spirits were moved and pleased, within the seas then was peace.

value.zh: 向使武帝復用弘羊之言，天下生靈皆盡之矣。
value.en: If Emperor Wu had again used Hongyang's words, all living beings under Heaven would have been exhausted.
value.literal: If formerly Emperor Wu had again used Hongyang's words, all living spirits under Heaven would have been exhausted.

value.zh: 是以光武中興，不逾蔥嶺，孝章即位，都護來歸。
value.en: Therefore Guangwu's restoration did not cross the Onion Range, and when Emperor Zhang assumed the throne, the Protector came to submit.
value.literal: Therefore Guangwu's restoration did not cross the Onion Range; when Emperor Zhang assumed the throne, the Protector came to submit.

value.zh: 南齊書卷第三 本紀第三
value.en: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 3, Annals 3
value.literal: Book of Southern Qi, Volume 3, Annals 3

value.zh: 十二月乙丑，以振威將軍陳僧授爲越州刺史。
value.en: Twelfth month, day yichou: Chen Sengshou, quelling-might general, took Yue.
value.literal: Twelfth month, day yichou: Quelling Might General Chen Sengshou was made Inspector of Yuezhou.

value.zh: 戊寅，詔「尚書丞郎職事繁劇，䘏俸未優，可量增賜祿。」
value.en: Day wuyin: an edict said, "The Masters of Writing and their aides bear heavy work for thin pay—raise their stipends as fits."
value.literal: Day wuyin, an edict said: "The directors and gentlemen of the Masters of Writing—their duties are dense and taxing, their stipends not generous—may receive measured increases in salary."

value.zh: 己卯，皇子子建爲湘東王。
value.en: Day jimao: the imperial prince Zijian was made king of Xiangdong.
value.literal: Day jimao: Imperial prince Zijian was made King of Xiangdong.

value.zh: 癸巳，以監青冀二州軍、行刺史事張沖爲青、冀二州刺史。
value.en: Day guisi: Zhang Chong, overseer of Qing and Ji and acting inspector, took Qing and Ji.
value.literal: Day guisi: Zhang Chong, overseer of Qing and Ji military affairs acting inspector, was made Inspector of Qing and Ji.

value.zh: 九年春正月甲午，以侍中江夏王鋒爲南徐州刺史，冠軍將軍劉悛爲益州刺史。
value.en: Year 9, spring, first month, day jiawu: Xiao Feng, prince of Jiangxia and palace attendant, took South Xu; Liu Min, champion general, took Yi.
value.literal: Year 9, spring, first month, day jiawu: Palace Attendant, Prince of Jiangxia Xiao Feng, was made Inspector of South Xuzhou; Champion General Liu Min was made Inspector of Yizhou.

value.zh: 辛丑，車駕祠南郊，詔「京師見囚繫，詳量原遣。」
value.en: Day xinchou: the emperor sacrificed at the southern suburb and ordered, "Review the prisoners in the capital and release them where mercy allows."
value.literal: Day xinchou: the imperial carriage worshipped at the southern suburb; an edict said: "Prisoners now held in the capital—consider carefully and release as appropriate."

value.zh: 夏四月乙亥，有司奏：「舊格一年兩過行陵，三月十五日曹郎以下小行，九月十五日司空以下大行。
value.en: Summer, fourth month, day yihai: the offices reported, "The old rule called for two tomb visits a year—the fifteenth of the third month, a minor visit for Masters of Writing gentlemen and below; the fifteenth of the ninth, a major visit for the Minister of Works and below.
value.literal: Summer, fourth month, day yihai: the relevant offices memorialized: "By the old rule there were two tomb visits a year—on the fifteenth of the third month a minor visit for gentlemen of the Masters of Writing and below, and on the fifteenth of the ninth month a major visit for the Minister of Works and below.

value.zh: 今長停小行，唯二州一大行。」
value.en: Suspend the minor visit for good; hold one major visit every two years."
value.literal: Now the minor visit is permanently suspended; only one major visit for the two provinces."

value.zh: 詔曰：「可。」
value.en: The edict said, "So be it."
value.literal: An edict said: "Approved."

value.zh: 秋九月戊辰，車駕幸琅邪城講武，觀者傾都，普頒酒肉。
value.en: Autumn, ninth month, day wuchen: the emperor reviewed arms at Langya; the city poured out to watch, and wine and meat were given to all.
value.literal: Autumn, ninth month, day wuchen: the imperial carriage visited Langya city for martial drill; the whole capital turned out to watch, and wine and meat were given broadly.

value.zh: 十年春正月戊午，詔「諸責負衆逋七年以前，悉原除。
value.en: Year 10, spring, first month, day wuwu: an edict said, "Every public and private debt seven years old or more is wiped clean.
value.literal: Year 10, spring, first month, day wuwu, an edict said: "All public and private debts seven years old or more are entirely remitted.

value.zh: 高貲不在例。
value.en: Usurious loans are excepted.
value.literal: High-interest loans are not included.

value.zh: 孤老六疾，人穀五斛。
value.en: Orphans, the aged, and the six classes of the sick receive five piculs of grain each.
value.literal: Orphans, the elderly, and the six kinds of affliction—five piculs of grain per person.

value.zh: 內外有務衆官增祿俸。」
value.en: Officials with heavy duties inside and outside the court get higher pay."
value.literal: All officials inside and outside with pressing duties receive increased stipends."

value.zh: 以左民尚書南平王銳爲湘州刺史，司徒竟陵王子良領尚書令，右衛將軍王玄邈爲北徐州刺史，中軍將軍廬陵王子卿進號車騎將軍，北中郎將南海王子罕爲兖州刺史，輔國將軍臨汝公昭文爲南豫州刺史，冠軍將軍王文和爲北兖州刺史。
value.en: Xiao Rui, prince of Nanping and minister for the people, took Xiang; Xiao Ziliang, prince of Jingling and minister over the masses, concurrently headed the Masters of Writing; Wang Xuanmiao, right guard general, took North Xu; Xiao Ziqing, prince of Luling and central army general, became general of chariots and cavalry; Xiao Zihan, prince of Nanhai and north bureau general, took Yan; Zhaowen, duke of Linru and supporter of the state, took South Yu; Wang Wenhe, champion general, took North Yan.
value.literal: Prince of Nanping Xiao Rui, Minister for the People, was made Inspector of Xiangzhou; Minister over the Masses, Prince of Jingling Xiao Ziliang, concurrently held Director of the Masters of Writing; Right Guard General Wang Xuanmiao was made Inspector of North Xuzhou; Central Army General, Prince of Luling Xiao Ziqing, was advanced to General of the Chariots and Cavalry; North Bureau General, Prince of Nanhai Xiao Zihan, was made Inspector of Yanzhou; Supporter of the State, Duke of Linru Zhaowen, was made Inspector of South Yuzhou; Champion General Wang Wenhe was made Inspector of North Yanzhou.

value.zh: 冬十月乙丑，車駕幸玄武湖講武。
value.en: Winter, tenth month, day yichou: the emperor drilled troops at Black Tortoise Lake.
value.literal: Winter, tenth month, day yichou: the imperial carriage visited the Black Tortoise Lake for martial drill.

value.zh: 甲午，車駕殷祠太廟。
value.en: Day jiawu: the emperor performed the close rite at the Imperial Temple.
value.literal: Day jiawu: the imperial carriage performed the close ancestral rite at the Imperial Temple.

value.zh: 十一月戊午，詔曰：「頃者霖雨，樵糧稍貴，京邑居民，多離其弊。
value.en: Eleventh month, day wuwu: an edict said, "These rains have driven up the price of fuel and grain; the capital's people are hard hit.
value.literal: Eleventh month, day wuwu, an edict said: "Lately the rains have made firewood and grain dear; residents of the capital suffer greatly.

value.zh: 遣中書舍人、二縣官長賑賜。」
value.en: Send palace secretaries and the magistrates of the two counties to give relief."
value.literal: Send Palace Secretaries and the magistrates of the two counties for relief grants."

value.zh: 十一年春正月癸丑，詔「京師見繫囚，詳所原遣」。
value.en: Year 11, spring, first month, day guichou: an edict said, "Every prisoner held in the capital is to be reviewed in detail for pardon and release."
value.literal: Year 11, spring, first month, day guichou: an edict said, "Prisoners held in the capital—examine them in detail for pardon and release."

value.zh: 以驃騎大將軍王敬則為司空，江州刺史鄱陽王鏘為領軍將軍，鎮軍大將軍陳顯達為江州刺史，右衞將軍崔慧景為豫州刺史。
value.en: Wang Jingze, grand general of agile cavalry, became minister of works; Xiao Qiang, king of Poyang and inspector of Jiangzhou, became leader of the army; Chen Xianda, pacifying-army grand general, took Jiangzhou; Cui Huijing, general of the right guard, took Yu.
value.literal: Grand General of Agile Cavalry Wang Jingze was made Minister of Works; Inspector of Jiangzhou Xiao Qiang, King of Poyang, was made Leader of the Army; Pacifying Army Grand General Chen Xianda was made Inspector of Jiangzhou; General of the Right Guard Cui Huijing was made Inspector of Yuzhou.

value.zh: 丙子，皇太子長懋薨。
value.en: Day bingzi: Crown Prince Changmao died.
value.literal: Day bingzi: Crown Prince Changmao died.

value.zh: 呂安國
value.en: Lu Anguo
value.literal: Lu Anguo

value.zh: 二年，虜寇邊，上遣安國出司州，安集民戶。
value.en: In the second year the northern enemy struck the border; the throne sent Anguo into Si to settle the people.
value.literal: In the second year the northerners raided the border; the emperor sent Anguo out to Si Province to settle the people and households.

value.zh: 詔曰：「郢、司之閒，流雜繁廣，宜竝加區判，定其隷屬。
value.en: An edict said: "Between Ying and Si the displaced are many and scattered; they should be sorted by district and their allegiance fixed.
value.literal: An edict said: 「Between Ying and Si, dispersed settlers are many and broad; they should all be marked off by district and their subordination fixed.

value.zh: 參詳兩州，事無專任，安國可蹔往經理。」
value.en: Look to both provinces: no one holds sole charge—Anguo may go for a time to put things in order."
value.literal: Review both provinces; no one bears sole charge—Anguo may go temporarily to oversee it.」

value.zh: 以本官使持節、總荊郢諸軍北討事，屯義陽西關。
value.en: At his present rank he was made envoy with credentials, overall commander of Jing and Ying for the northern campaign, and camped at Yiyang's western pass.
value.literal: With his existing rank, envoy with credentials, overall commander of Jing and Ying military affairs for the northern campaign, encamped at Yiyang's western pass.

value.zh: 虜未至，安國移屯沔口以俟應接。
value.en: The enemy never came; Anguo shifted camp to the mouth of the Mian to stand ready for relief.
value.literal: The enemy did not come; Anguo moved his camp to the Mian mouth to await support.

value.zh: 改封湘郷。
value.en: He was re-enfeoffed at Xiangxiang.
value.literal: He was re-enfeoffed at Xiangxiang.

value.zh: 世祖卽位，授使持節、散騎常侍、平西將軍、司州刺史，領義陽太守，
value.en: When Emperor Wu took the throne he received credentials as envoy, supernumerary attendant of scattered cavalry, General Who Pacifies the West, and inspector of Si, still holding Yiyang as administrator.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne he was granted envoy with credentials, supernumerary attendant of scattered cavalry, General Who Pacifies the West, inspector of Si Province, still administrator of Yiyang,

value.zh: 永明二年，徙都督南兖兖徐青冀五州諸軍事、平北將軍、南兖州刺史，仍爲都督、湘州刺史。
value.en: In the second year of Yongming, he was then made overseer of South Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji, General Who Pacifies the North and inspector of South Yan, while still overseeing Xiang as inspector.
value.literal: In the second year of Yongming, he was moved to oversee South Yan, Yan, Xu, Qing, and Ji military affairs, General Who Pacifies the North, inspector of South Yan; still overseer and inspector of Xiangzhou.

value.zh: 四年，湘川蠻動，安國督州兵討之。
value.en: In the fourth year the tribes of Xiang rose; Anguo led provincial troops to put them down.
value.literal: In the fourth year Xiangxiang barbarians stirred; Anguo oversaw provincial troops to suppress them.

value.zh: 有疾，徵爲光祿大夫，加散騎常侍。
value.en: Illness brought him to court as Grandee of Splendid Happiness with added supernumerary attendant of scattered cavalry.
value.literal: He fell ill and was summoned as Grandee of Splendid Happiness, with added supernumerary attendant of scattered cavalry.

value.zh: 安國欣有文授，謂其子曰：「汝後勿作褶驅使，單衣猶恨不稱，當爲朱衣官也。」
value.en: Anguo rejoiced that his sons had learning; he told his son: "Hereafter do not serve as a pleated-coat driver—even plain robes still feel unworthy; you should wear vermilion and hold office."
value.literal: Anguo delighted that he had literary learning for his sons; he told his son: 「After me do not become a pleated-coat driver; plain dress still seems not fitting—you should be a vermilion-robed official.」

value.zh: 上遣中書舍人茹法亮敕安國曰：「吾恒憂卿疾病，應有所須，勿致難也。」
value.en: The emperor sent Secretarial Attendant Ru Faliang to tell Anguo: "I always fret over your sickness; if you need anything, do not hold back."
value.literal: The emperor sent Secretarial Attendant Ru Faliang to instruct Anguo: 「I constantly worry over your illness; should you need anything, do not make it difficult.」

value.zh: 明年，遷都官尚書，領太子左率。
value.en: The next year he was made minister of justice and led the crown prince's left guard.
value.literal: The next year he was moved to Minister of Justice, leading the crown prince's left guard.

value.zh: 六年，遷領軍將軍。
value.en: In the sixth year he was made General of the Army.
value.literal: In the sixth year he was moved to General of the Army.

value.zh: 安國累居將率，在朝以宿舊見遇。
value.en: Anguo had long stood at the head of armies; at court he was honored as an old companion.
value.literal: Anguo long held command ranks; in court he was treated as an elder of long standing.

value.zh: 尋遷散騎常侍、金紫光祿大夫、兖州中正，給扶。
value.en: Soon he was raised to supernumerary attendant of scattered cavalry, household minister with golden seal and purple ribbon, and impartial nominee for Yan, with attendants to lean on.
value.literal: Soon he was moved to supernumerary attendant of scattered cavalry, Household Minister with golden seal and purple ribbon, impartial nominee for Yan Province, with support staff provided.

value.zh: 上又敕茹法亮曰：「吾見呂安國疾狀，自不宜勞，且脚中旣恒惡，扶人至吾前，於禮望殊成有虧，吾難敕之。
value.en: The emperor again told Ru Faliang: "I have read Lu Anguo's medical notes—he is plainly unfit for exertion; his feet have long troubled him, and to be led before me would shame his standing in ritual; I cannot bring myself to command it.
value.literal: The emperor again instructed Ru Faliang: 「I have seen Lu Anguo's medical reports—by himself he is unfit for labor; moreover his feet have long been bad, and to be helped before me is a great loss to ceremonial bearing; I find it hard to order him.

value.zh: 其人甚諱病，卿可作私意向，其若好差不復須扶人，依例入，幸勿牽勉。」
value.en: He hides his sickness deeply; speak to him privately—if he improves enough to walk unaided, let him come in as usual; do not force him."
value.literal: The man greatly hides his illness; you may make a private inquiry—if he is somewhat better and no longer needs support, let him enter by precedent; do not press him.」

value.zh: 八年，卒，年六十四。
value.en: In the eighth year he died, at sixty-four.
value.literal: In the eighth year he died, at age sixty-four.

value.zh: 贈使持節、鎮北將軍、南兖州刺史，常侍如故。
value.en: Posthumously he was granted credentials as envoy, General Who Guards the North, and inspector of South Yan, with attendant rank unchanged.
value.literal: Posthumously granted envoy with credentials, General Who Guards the North, inspector of South Yan Province, attendant as before.

value.zh: 給鼓吹一部。
value.en: He was given one suite of martial music.
value.literal: Given one set of martial music instruments.

value.zh: 諡肅侯。
value.en: His posthumous title was Marquis Su.
value.literal: Posthumous title Marquis Su.

value.zh: 列傳第七
value.en: the seventh year of Biographies
value.literal: Biographies 7

value.zh: 五年，武帝伐慕容超，除中軍諮議參軍，與兗州刺史劉藩大破超軍，進圍廣固，屢獻規略。
value.en: the fifth year of In, campaigning against Murong Chao, Jingxuan became an advising aide in the central army; with Liu Fan of Yanzhou he routed Chao and besieged Guanggu, offering strategy at every turn.
value.literal: In the fifth year Emperor Wu attacked Murong Chao; Jingxuan was made advising aide in the central army and with Yanzhou Inspector Liu Fan greatly defeated Chao's army, advanced to besiege Guanggu, and repeatedly offered plans.

value.zh: 盧循逼建鄴，敬宣分領鮮卑獸斑突騎，置陣甚整。
value.en: When Lu Xun threatened Jiankang, Jingxuan led Xianbei cavalry with spotted mounts and drew up an impeccable line.
value.literal: When Lu Xun pressed Jiankang Jingxuan separately commanded Xianbei beast-spotted shock cavalry and set the formation very orderly.

value.zh: 循走，仍從南討，為左衛將軍。
value.en: After Xun fled he continued south and was made General of the Left Guard.
value.literal: Xun fled; he still followed the southern campaign and became General of the Left Guard.

value.zh: 敬宣寬厚，善待士，多伎藝，弓馬音律，無事不善。
value.en: Generous and gracious to men of talent, he mastered archery, horsemanship, music—there was scarcely an art he could not handle.
value.literal: Jingxuan was generous, treated scholars well, and had many skills—in archery, horsemanship, and music there was nothing he did not excel at.

value.zh: 尚書僕射謝混美才地，少所交納，與敬宣遇便盡禮。
value.en: Xie Hun, vice director of the secretariat, seldom befriended anyone, yet with Jingxuan he was immediately cordial.
value.literal: Secretary Deputy Director Xie Hun had fine talent and standing and rarely made new acquaintances; with Jingxuan he at once showed full courtesy.

value.zh: 或問混：「卿未嘗輕交，而傾蓋劉壽，何也？」
value.en: Someone asked Hun, "You rarely open up to people—why this instant bond with Liu Shou?"
value.literal: Someone asked Hun, "You have never lightly befriended anyone, yet you treat Liu Shou with open arms—why?"

value.zh: 混曰：「孔文舉禮太史子義，天下豈有非之邪。」
value.en: Hun replied, "When Kong Wenju honored Taishi Ziyi, who in the realm criticized him?"
value.literal: Hun said, "Kong Wenju honored Taishi Ziyi—did anyone under heaven fault him for it?"

value.zh: 初，敬宣蜀還，劉毅欲以重法繩之。
value.en: When Jingxuan came back from Shu, Liu Yi wanted him punished severely.
value.literal: At first, when Jingxuan returned from Shu, Liu Yi wanted to punish him by heavy law.

value.zh: 武帝既相任待，又何無忌謂不宜以私憾傷至公。
value.en: The emperor already relied on him, and He Wuji argued that private spite must not override the public good.
value.literal: The Emperor already trusted and employed him, and He Wuji said one should not let private resentment harm supreme fairness.

value.zh: 毅雖止，猶謂武帝曰：「平生之舊，豈可孤信？
value.en: Yi desisted, yet told the emperor, "A companion of long standing—can you trust him blindly?
value.literal: Although Yi stopped, he still said to the Emperor, "An old friend of many years—can he be trusted alone?

value.zh: 光武悔之于龐萌，曹公失之于孟卓。
value.en: Emperor Guangwu regretted trusting Pang Meng; Cao Cao was betrayed by Zhang Miao.
value.literal: Emperor Guangwu regretted Pang Meng; Cao Cao lost out with Meng Zhuo.

value.zh: 宜深慎之。」
value.en: You should be very careful."
value.literal: You should be deeply cautious."

value.zh: 毅出為荊州，謂敬宣曰：「欲屈卿為長史、南蠻，豈有見輔意乎？」
value.en: Posted to Jing Province, Yi told Jingxuan, "I want you as chief aide and commander of the southern barbarians—will you serve under me?"
value.literal: Yi went out to Jing Province and said to Jingxuan, "I wish to appoint you chief aide and southern barbarian commander—do you mean to assist me?"

value.zh: 敬宣懼禍，以告武帝。
value.en: Fearing a trap, Jingxuan reported this to the emperor.
value.literal: Jingxuan feared disaster and told the Emperor.

value.zh: 帝笑曰：「但令老兄平安，必無過慮。」
value.en: The emperor laughed: "So long as your old friend keeps his head, you have nothing to fear."
value.literal: The Emperor laughed and said, "Only let your old brother stay safe and you need not worry too much."

value.zh: 後領冀州刺史。
value.en: Later Jingxuan became inspector of Ji Province.
value.literal: Later he held the post of Inspector of Ji Province.

value.zh: 時帝西討劉毅，豫州刺史諸葛長人監太尉軍事，貽敬宣書曰：「盤龍狼戾專恣，自取夷滅。
value.en: While the emperor marched west against Liu Yi, Zhuge Changren of Yuzhou, overseeing the grand marshal's armies, wrote Jingxuan: "Panlong's arrogance destroyed him.
value.literal: When the Emperor campaigned west against Liu Yi, Yuzhou Inspector Zhuge Changren supervised the Grand Marshal's military affairs and wrote Jingxuan, "Panlong was wolfish, wilful, and brought ruin on himself.

value.zh: 異端將盡，世路方夷，富貴之事，相與共之。」
value.en: The rebel faction is almost finished and better days lie ahead—let us share the rewards together."
value.literal: The strange branch is nearly gone and the world's path is clearing; matters of wealth and honor let us share them."

value.zh: 敬宣報曰：「下官常懼福過災生，實思避盈居損。
value.en: Jingxuan answered, "I have always feared that good luck invites disaster and sought to stay modest rather than grasp for more.
value.literal: Jingxuan replied, "This humble officer has always feared fortune outrunning merit and truly wishes to avoid fullness and dwell in modesty.

value.zh: 富貴之旨，非所敢當。」
value.en: I dare not accept such an offer of rank and riches."
value.literal: The intent of wealth and honor is not what I dare accept."

value.zh: 便以長人書呈，帝謂王誕曰：「阿壽故為不負我。」
value.en: He forwarded Changren's letter at once; the emperor told Wang Dan, "A Shou has not let me down."
value.literal: He at once presented Changren's letter; the Emperor said to Wang Dan, "A Shou truly does not fail me."

value.zh: 十一年，進號右軍將軍。
value.en: the eleventh year of In he was promoted to General of the Right Army.
value.literal: In the eleventh year he advanced in title to General of the Right Army.

value.zh: 時晉宗室司馬道賜為敬宣參軍。
value.en: Jin imperial clansman Sima Daosi then served on Jingxuan's staff.
value.literal: At that time Jin clansman Sima Daosi was Jingxuan's staff officer.

value.zh: 會武帝西征司馬休之，而道賜乃陰結同府辟閭道秀、左右小將王猛子等謀反。
value.en: During the western campaign against Sima Xiuzhi, Daosi secretly conspired with staff officer Pilu Daoxiu and aides Wang Mengzi and others.
value.literal: When the Emperor campaigned west against Sima Xiuzhi, Daosi secretly joined staff member Pilu Daoxiu and junior officers Wang Mengzi and others in plotting rebellion.

value.zh: 道賜自號齊王，規據廣固，舉兵應休之。
value.en: Daosi proclaimed himself Prince of Qi, aimed to seize Guanggu, and mustered forces for Xiuzhi.
value.literal: Daosi styled himself Prince of Qi, planned to hold Guanggu, and raised troops to support Xiuzhi.

value.zh: 猛子取敬宣刀殺敬宣，文武佐吏即討道賜、道秀、猛子斬之。
value.en: Mengzi seized Jingxuan's sword and killed him; staff and officers immediately executed Daosi, Daoxiu, and Mengzi.
value.literal: Mengzi took Jingxuan's sword and killed Jingxuan; civil and military aides at once punished Daosi, Daoxiu, and Mengzi and beheaded them.

value.zh: 先是敬宣嘗夜與僚佐宴，空中有投一隻芒屩於坐，墜敬宣食盤上，長三尺五寸，已經人著，耳鼻間並欲壞，頃之而敗。
value.en: Once at a night feast with his officers, a worn straw sandal three feet five inches long—reeking of a human wearer—dropped from nowhere into his dish; not long after he was killed.
value.literal: Earlier Jingxuan had once feasted at night with his staff; from the air someone threw a single straw sandal onto the seat—it fell into Jingxuan's food tray, three chi five cun long, already worn by a person, nose and ears nearly ruined—and soon after he was destroyed.

value.zh: 喪至，武帝臨哭甚哀。
value.en: When the bier arrived the emperor mourned him in person, deeply grieved.
value.literal: When the coffin arrived the Emperor came in person to mourn, very sorrowful.

value.zh: 子光祖嗣。
value.en: His son Guangzu succeeded him.
value.literal: His son Guangzu inherited.

value.zh: 宋受禪，國除。
value.en: When Song took the throne the enfeoffment lapsed.
value.literal: When Song received the abdication the fief was abolished.

value.zh: 劉懷肅，彭城人，宋武帝從母兄也。
value.en: Liu Huaisu of Pengcheng was the emperor's cousin on his mother's side.
value.literal: Liu Huaisu was a man of Pengcheng, maternal elder cousin to Song Emperor Wu.

value.zh: 家世貧窶，而躬耕好學。
value.en: Though his family was poor he farmed himself and loved study.
value.literal: The family had long been poor, yet he personally plowed and loved learning.

value.zh: 仕晉為費令。
value.en: Under Jin he served as magistrate of Fei county.
value.literal: He served Jin as magistrate of Fei.

value.zh: 及聞武帝起義，棄縣來奔。
value.en: Hearing the emperor had risen in arms, he abandoned his post and rushed to join him.
value.literal: When he heard the Emperor had raised the banner of revolt he abandoned his county and came to join.

value.zh: 懷肅次弟懷敬，澀訥無才能。
value.en: Huaisu's younger brother Huaijing was slow of speech and lacked ability.
value.literal: Huaisu's next younger brother Huaijing was dull-spoken and without talent.

value.zh: 初，武帝產而皇妣殂，孝皇帝貧薄，無由得乳人，議欲不舉，帝從母生懷敬，未期，乃斷懷敬乳而自養帝。
value.en: When the future emperor was born his mother died; the household was too poor for a wet nurse and nearly abandoned the infant until his aunt, still nursing Huaijing, weaned her own son to feed him.
value.literal: At first when the Emperor was born the imperial mother died; Emperor Xiao was poor and had no wet nurse; they debated not raising the child; the Emperor's maternal aunt bore Huaijing, not yet weaned, so she stopped Huaijing's milk and nursed the Emperor herself.

value.zh: 帝以舊恩，懷敬累見寵授，至會稽太守。
value.en: Out of gratitude for that old debt the emperor kept advancing Huaijing until he became administrator of Kuaiji.
value.literal: Because of the old kindness the Emperor repeatedly favored Huaijing, reaching Administrator of Kuaiji.

value.zh: 時以為速，武帝曰：「亡姨于我恩重，此何可忘？」
value.en: Critics called the promotions too swift; the emperor said, "My aunt's kindness was profound—how could I forget it?"
value.literal: People then thought it too fast; the Emperor said, "My late aunt's kindness to me was heavy—how could this be forgotten?"

value.zh: 曆尚書，金紫光祿大夫。
value.en: He went on to serve as minister of the masters of writing and as grand master with the gold seal and purple ribbon.
value.literal: He served as Minister of the Masters of Writing and as Grand Master of the Gold Seal and Purple Ribbon.

value.zh: 及盧循逼都，孟昶等議奉天子過江，進廷議不可，面折昶等，武帝甚嘉之。
value.en: When Lu Xun threatened the capital Meng Chang urged evacuating the emperor across the river; Jin argued against it in open court and won the emperor's praise.
value.literal: When Lu Xun pressed the capital Meng Chang and others debated escorting the Son of Heaven across the river; Jin spoke in court that this could not be and openly refuted Chang and the rest; the Emperor greatly praised him.

value.zh: 除鄱陽太守。
value.en: He was appointed administrator of Poyang.
value.literal: He was made Administrator of Poyang.

value.zh: 後隨劉藩斬徐道覆。
value.en: He later joined Liu Fan in killing Xu Daofu.
value.literal: Later he followed Liu Fan in beheading Xu Daofu.

value.zh: 義熙九年，以前後功，封望蔡縣男。
value.en: In the ninth year of Yixi he received the barony of Wangcai for lifetime service.
value.literal: In the ninth year of Yixi, for former and later merit, he was enfeoffed Baron of Wangcai.

value.zh: 永初二年，累遷太子右衛率。
value.en: In the second year of Yongchu he rose to right commandant of the heir's guard.
value.literal: In the second year of Yongchu he rose repeatedly to Right Commandant of the Heir's Guard.

value.zh: 卒，追論討司馬休之功，進爵為子。
value.en: After death his campaign against Sima Xiuzhi was remembered and he was raised posthumously to viscount.
value.literal: On death his merit against Sima Xiuzhi was recalled and he was advanced to viscount.

value.zh: 傳國至曾孫，齊受禪，國除。
value.en: The fief passed to a great-grandson; when Qi took the throne it lapsed.
value.literal: The fief passed to a great-grandson; when Qi received the abdication the fief was abolished.

value.zh: 孟懷玉，平昌安丘人也，世居京口。
value.en: Meng Huaiyu of Anqiu in Pingchang came from a Jingkou family.
value.literal: Meng Huaiyu was a man of Anqiu in Pingchang and for generations resided at Jingkou.

value.zh: 宋武帝東伐孫恩，以為建武司馬。
value.en: When the emperor marched east against Sun En he became marshal of the army that established might.
value.literal: When Song Emperor Wu campaigned east against Sun En he was made marshal of the army that established might.

value.zh: 豫義旗，從平京口，定建鄴，以功封鄱陽縣五等侯。
value.en: He joined the revolt, helped take Jingkou and Jiankang, and received the fifth-rank marquisate of Poyang.
value.literal: He joined the banner of righteousness, followed in pacifying Jingkou and settling Jiankang, and for merit was enfeoffed Fifth-rank Marquis of Poyang.

value.zh: 盧循逼都，以戰功為中軍諮議參軍。
value.en: When Lu Xun threatened the capital he became an advising aide in the central army for battlefield merit.
value.literal: When Lu Xun pressed the capital, for battle merit he was made advising aide in the central army.

value.zh: 循平，封陽豐縣男，位江州刺史、南中郎將。
value.en: After Xun's defeat he became baron of Yangfeng, inspector of Jiangzhou, and General of the Southern Gentlemen.
value.literal: When Xun was pacified he was enfeoffed Baron of Yangfeng, and held the posts of Inspector of Jiangzhou and General of the Southern Gentlemen.

value.zh: 卒官。
value.en: He died in office.
value.literal: He died in office.

value.zh: 無子，國除。
value.en: He left no sons and the fief lapsed.
value.literal: Without sons the fief was abolished.

value.zh: 懷玉弟龍符，驍果有膽氣，早為武帝所知，以軍功封平昌縣五等子。
value.en: Huaiyu's brother Longfu was daring and fierce; known early to the emperor, he earned the fifth-rank viscounty of Pingchang.
value.literal: Huaiyu's younger brother Longfu was fierce and bold with courage; the Emperor knew him early and for military merit enfeoffed him Fifth-rank Viscount of Pingchang.

value.zh: 從伐廣固，以車騎參軍加龍驤將軍、廣川太守。
value.en: At Guanggu he served as chariot aide, Flying Dragon General, and administrator of Guangchuan.
value.literal: Following the Guanggu campaign he was chariot-and-horse aide plus Flying Dragon General and Administrator of Guangchuan.

value.zh: 乘勝追奔，被圍見害，追贈青州刺史，封臨沅縣男。
value.en: Pursuing fleeing enemies he was surrounded and killed; posthumously he became inspector of Qingzhou and baron of Linjiang.
value.literal: Pursuing the rout he was surrounded and killed; posthumously he was given Inspector of Qingzhou and enfeoffed Baron of Linjiang.

value.zh: 藩轉參太尉大將軍相國軍事。
value.en: Fan moved to staff duty under the grand marshal and chancellor.
value.literal: Fan was transferred to staff officer on the Grand Marshal's and Chancellor's military affairs.

value.zh: 宋武帝起兵，玄戰敗將出奔，藩扣馬曰：「今羽林射手猶有八百，皆是義故西人，一旦舍此，欲歸可復得乎？」
value.en: When the emperor rose, Xuan prepared to flee; Fan grabbed his bridle: "You still have eight hundred western archers—leave now and you can never come back."
value.literal: When Song Emperor Wu raised troops Xuan was defeated and about to flee; Fan seized his horse and said, "The palace archers still number eight hundred—all old followers from the west; once you abandon this, can you ever return?"

value.zh: 玄直以鞭指天而已。
value.en: Xuan only gestured skyward with his whip.
value.literal: Xuan merely pointed heavenward with his whip.

value.zh: 於是奔散相失，追及玄於蕪湖。
value.en: They scattered in chaos; Fan caught Xuan again at Wuhu.
value.literal: Thereupon they scattered and lost one another; he caught up with Xuan at Wuhu.

value.zh: 玄見藩喜謂張須無曰：「卿州故為多士，今復見王修。」
value.en: Seeing Fan, Xuan told Zhang Xu Wu, "Your region breeds real men—here is Wang Xiu again."
value.literal: Xuan saw Fan and said joyfully to Zhang Xu Wu, "Your province truly breeds many scholars—now I see Wang Xiu again."

value.zh: 桑落之敗，藩艦被燒，並鎧入水，潛行三十許步，方得登岸。
value.en: At Sangluo his ship burned; armored, he swam thirty paces underwater before reaching shore.
value.literal: At the defeat of Sangluo Fan's ship was burned; wearing armor he entered the water and stole thirty paces before he could climb ashore.

value.zh: 乃還家。
value.en: He went home.
value.literal: He then returned home.

value.zh: 武帝素聞藩直言于殷氏，又為玄盡節，召參鎮軍軍事。
value.en: The emperor, knowing Fan had warned Yin and served Xuan faithfully, summoned him to the pacifying army staff.
value.literal: The Emperor had long heard Fan's blunt words to the Yin clan and his full loyalty to Xuan; he summoned him to staff the army that pacifies the army.

value.zh: 從征慕容超，超軍屯聚臨朐。
value.en: Campaigning against Murong Chao, he found Chao's army massed at Linqu.
value.literal: Following the campaign against Murong Chao, Chao's army gathered at Linqu.

value.zh: 藩言于武帝曰：「賊屯軍城外，留守必寡，今往取其城而斬其旗幟，此韓信所以克趙也。」
value.en: Fan told the emperor, "They camp outside—the city is empty; seize it and strike down their flags, as Han Xin did at Zhao."
value.literal: Fan said to the Emperor, "The bandits camp outside the city—the garrison must be thin; go now, take the city and cut down their banners—this is how Han Xin conquered Zhao."

value.zh: 帝乃遣檀韶與藩潛往，即克其城。
value.en: The emperor sent Tan Shao and Fan by stealth and they captured it at once.
value.literal: The Emperor then sent Tan Shao and Fan secretly; they at once took the city.

value.zh: 賊見城陷，一時奔走，還保廣固。
value.en: Seeing the city lost, the enemy fled back to Guanggu.
value.literal: The bandits saw the city fall and at once fled, returning to hold Guanggu.

value.zh: 圍之，將拔之夜，忽有鳥大如鵝，蒼黑色，飛入帝帳裏，眾以為不祥。
value.en: On the eve of victory a goose-sized dark bird flew into the imperial tent; men took it for a bad sign.
value.literal: Besieging it, on the night it was about to fall suddenly a bird large as a goose, dark blue-black, flew into the Emperor's tent; the crowd thought it ill-omened.

value.zh: 藩賀曰：「蒼黑者，胡虜色。
value.en: Fan declared, "Dark blue is the barbarians' color.
value.literal: Fan congratulated him, "Dark blue is the color of the barbarians.

value.zh: 胡虜歸我，大吉之祥。」
value.en: Their surrender is a great omen."
value.literal: Barbarians returning to us is a great auspice."

value.zh: 明旦攻城，陷之。
value.en: At dawn they stormed the city and took it.
value.literal: At dawn he attacked the city and took it.

value.zh: 從討盧循于左裏，頻戰有功，封吳平縣五等子。
value.en: Fighting Lu Xun at Zuoli he won repeated honors and received the fifth-rank viscounty of Wuping.
value.literal: Following the punitive action against Lu Xun at Zuoli he repeatedly won merit and was enfeoffed Fifth-rank Viscount of Wuping.

value.zh: 尋除鄱陽太守，從伐劉毅。
value.en: He soon became administrator of Poyang and marched against Liu Yi.
value.literal: Soon he was made Administrator of Poyang and followed the campaign against Liu Yi.

value.zh: 初，毅當之荊州，表求東道還建鄴辭墓。
value.en: When Yi left for Jing Province he asked to swing by Jiankang to mourn at his family tombs.
value.literal: At first when Yi was going to Jing Province he memorialized asking to travel the eastern route back to Jiankang to visit his ancestors' tombs.

value.zh: 去都數十里，不過拜闕。
value.en: He stopped tens of li from court without paying homage at the palace.
value.literal: Several tens of li from the capital he did not pass to bow at the palace.

value.zh: 帝出倪塘會毅，藩請殺之，乃謂帝曰：「公謂劉衛軍為公下乎？」
value.en: The emperor met Yi at Nitang; Fan urged killing him: "Do you think Defender Liu serves under you?"
value.literal: The Emperor went out to Nitang to meet Yi; Fan asked to kill him and said to the Emperor, "Do you think Defender Liu serves under you?"

value.zh: 帝曰：「卿謂何如？」
value.en: The emperor asked, "What do you think?"
value.literal: The Emperor said, "What do you think?"

value.zh: 對曰：「夫豁達大度，功高天下，連百萬之眾，允天人之望，毅固以此服公。
value.en: Fan answered, "Your breadth and achievement command the realm—Yi submits to that.
value.literal: He replied, "Broad-minded and magnanimous, merit high under heaven, commanding millions, fulfilling heaven and men's hopes—Yi for this submits to you.

value.zh: 至於涉獵記傳，一詠一談，自許以雄豪，加以誇伐，搢紳白麵之士，輻湊而歸，此毅不肯為公下也。」
value.en: But his salons, his poetry, his swagger—scholars flock to him. That is Yi refusing to serve under you."
value.literal: As for browsing records and histories, reciting and conversing, styling himself a hero and adding boast—gentry and pale-faced scholars flock to him; this is Yi refusing to serve under you."

value.zh: 帝曰：「吾與毅俱有克復功，其過未彰，不可自相圖。」
value.en: The emperor said, "We both restored the dynasty; his disloyalty is not yet proven—we cannot turn on each other."
value.literal: The Emperor said, "Yi and I both have merit in restoration; his fault is not yet clear—we cannot plot against each other."

value.zh: 至是謂藩曰：「昔從卿倪塘之謀，無今舉也。」
value.en: Now he told Fan, "If I had listened at Nitang I would not need this war."
value.literal: Now he said to Fan, "Had I followed your Nitang counsel there would be no present campaign."

value.zh: 又從征司馬休之，復為參軍。
value.en: He again campaigned against Sima Xiuzhi as a staff officer.
value.literal: He again followed the campaign against Sima Xiuzhi and again served as staff officer.

value.zh: 徐逵之敗沒，帝怒，即日於馬頭岸度江。
value.en: After Xu Daizhi's defeat the furious emperor crossed the Yangzi that same day at Matou.
value.literal: When Xu Daizhi was defeated and lost the Emperor was angry and that same day crossed the Yangzi at Matou bank.

value.zh: 江津岸壁立數丈，休之臨岸置陣，無由可登。
value.en: The bank rose sheer for yards; Xiuzhi lined the top and offered no foothold.
value.literal: The river crossing's bank was a cliff several zhang; Xiuzhi set battle lines on the bank with no way to climb.

value.zh: 帝呼藩令上，藩有疑色。
value.en: The emperor ordered Fan up; Fan hesitated.
value.literal: The Emperor called Fan to ascend; Fan showed hesitation.

value.zh: 帝怒，命左右錄來，欲斬之。
value.en: Enraged, the emperor had him seized for execution.
value.literal: The Emperor in anger ordered attendants to seize him and was about to behead him.

value.zh: 藩不受命，顧曰：「寧前死耳。」
value.en: Fan refused and said, "I would rather die advancing."
value.literal: Fan would not obey the order and looked back, saying, "Better die going forward."

value.zh: 以刀頭穿岸，劣容腳指徑上，隨之者稍多。
value.en: He dug toeholds with his sword tip and climbed; others followed.
value.literal: He pierced the bank with the sword-point, barely fitting his toes, and went up; those who followed gradually increased.

value.zh: 及登，殊死戰，敗之。
value.en: At the top they fought desperately and routed Xiuzhi.
