value.literal: Once atop they fought to the death and defeated the enemy.

value.zh: 從伐關中，參太尉軍事，統別軍至河東。
value.en: On the Guanzhong expedition he led a detached force to Hedong under the grand marshal.
value.literal: Following the Guanzhong expedition he was staff officer on the Grand Marshal's military affairs, commanding a separate army to Hedong.

value.zh: 暴風漂輜重艦度北岸，魏軍牽得此艦。
value.en: A storm blew a supply ship to the north bank where Wei seized it.
value.literal: A gale blew supply ships across to the north bank; Wei troops towed away this ship.

value.zh: 藩氣憤，率左右十二人乘小船徑往。
value.en: Furious, Fan took twelve men in a skiff straight after it.
value.literal: Fan in fury led twelve men in a small boat straight there.

value.zh: 魏騎五六百，見藩來並笑之。
value.en: Five or six hundred Wei cavalry saw him and laughed.
value.literal: Five or six hundred Wei horsemen saw Fan coming and all laughed at him.

value.zh: 藩素善射，登岸射之，應弦而倒者十許人。
value.en: A fine archer, he shot from shore and dropped a dozen at once.
value.literal: Fan had long been skilled at archery; ashore he shot them and over ten fell at the twang of the string.

value.zh: 魏軍皆退，悉收所失而反。
value.en: The Wei riders fled and he recovered everything.
value.literal: The Wei army all retreated and he fully recovered what was lost and returned.

value.zh: 又遣藩及朱超石等追魏軍於半城，魏騎數萬合圍，藩及超石不盈五千，力戰，大破之。
value.en: He sent Fan and Zhu Chao shi after Wei at Bancheng; though surrounded by tens of thousands with fewer than five thousand men they smashed the enemy.
value.literal: He again sent Fan and Zhu Chao shi and others to pursue Wei forces at Bancheng; tens of thousands of Wei horsemen surrounded them; Fan and Chao shi had fewer than five thousand and fought fiercely, greatly defeating them.

value.zh: 武帝還彭城，參相國軍事。
value.en: Back at Pengcheng he joined the chancellor's staff.
value.literal: When the Emperor returned to Pengcheng he served on the Chancellor's military staff.

value.zh: 論平司馬休之及廣固功，封陽山縣男。
value.en: For Xiuzhi and Guanggu he received the barony of Yangshan.
value.literal: Recalling merit in pacifying Sima Xiuzhi and at Guanggu he was enfeoffed Baron of Yangshan.

value.zh: 元嘉中，位太子左衛率。
value.en: In Yuanjia he became left commandant of the heir's guard.
value.literal: In Yuanjia he reached Left Commandant of the Heir's Guard.

value.zh: 卒，諡曰壯侯。
value.en: His posthumous title was Marquis Zhuang.
value.literal: On death posthumous title Marquis Zhuang.

value.zh: 子隆世嗣。
value.en: Longshi succeeded him.
value.literal: Longshi succeeded.

value.zh: 李安人
value.en: Li Anren
value.literal: Li Anren

value.zh: 祖嶷，衛軍將軍。
value.en: His grandfather Yi served as General of the Guards.
value.literal: His grandfather Yi was General of the Guards.

value.zh: 父欽之，薛令。
value.en: His father Qinzhi served as magistrate of Xue.
value.literal: His father Qinzhi was magistrate of Xue.

value.zh: 沈攸之事起，高帝入朝堂，遣僧靜將腹心先至石頭經略袁粲。
value.en: When Shen Youzhi rebelled, Emperor Gao went to court and sent Dai Sengjing with his closest followers to secure Stone City against Yuan Can.
value.literal: When Shen Youzhi's affair arose, the Emperor Gao entered the audience hall and sent Sengjing with his trusted men ahead to Stone City to deal with Yuan Can.

value.zh: 時蘇烈據倉城門，僧靜射書與烈，夜縋入城。
value.en: Su Lie then held Cangcheng Gate. Dai Sengjing shot an arrow bearing a message to Lie and was hauled over the wall at night.
value.literal: At that time Su Lie held Cangcheng Gate; Sengjing shot a letter to Lie and was lowered into the city by rope at night.

value.zh: 粲登城西南門，列燭火坐，台軍至射之，火乃滅。
value.en: Yuan Can took the southwest gate, set out rows of candles, and sat; when the imperial troops shot, every flame died.
value.literal: Can mounted the southwest gate of the city, arrayed candles and sat; when the palace troops arrived and shot, the flames went out.

value.zh: 回登東門，其党孫曇瓘驍勇善戰，每蕩一合，輒大殺傷，官軍死者百餘人。
value.en: He went back to the east gate. His ally Sun Tanxun fought with terrifying skill: every clash left a great heap of dead, and over a hundred imperial soldiers fell.
value.literal: He returned to the east gate; his partisan Sun Tanxun was fierce and skilled in battle—each time he swept through a formation he inflicted heavy slaughter, and more than a hundred government soldiers died.

value.zh: 軍主王天生殊死拒戰，故得相持。
value.en: Commander Wang Tiansheng held him off with suicidal courage, and the fight hung in balance.
value.literal: The army commander Wang Tiansheng resisted with desperate valor, and thus they were able to stalemate each other.

value.zh: 自亥至醜，有流星赤色照地墜城中，僧靜率力攻倉門，手斬粲於東門，外軍燒門入。
value.en: From hai to chou a crimson meteor flamed down into the city. Dai Sengjing stormed Cang Gate, cut down Yuan Can with his own hand at the east gate, and the outer force burned its way in.
value.literal: From the hai hour to the chou hour a crimson meteor blazed to the ground inside the city; Sengjing led his force in assault on Cang Gate, personally beheaded Can at the east gate, and the outer army burned the gate and entered.

value.zh: 以功除前軍將軍、甯朔將軍。
value.en: For this service he was made General of the Vanguard and General Who Pacifies the North.
value.literal: For his merit he was appointed General of the Vanguard and General Who Pacifies the North.

value.zh: 高帝即位，封建昌縣侯，位太子左衛率。
value.en: When Emperor Gao ascended the throne, Sengjing was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jianchang County and held the office of Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guards.
value.literal: When Emperor Gao ascended the throne, Sengjing was enfeoffed as Marquis of Jianchang County and held the office of Left Commandant of the Heir Apparent's Guards.

value.zh: 武帝踐阼，出為北徐州刺史。
value.en: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Sengjing went out as Inspector of Northern Xuzhou.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Sengjing went out as Inspector of Northern Xuzhou.

value.zh: 買牛給貧人令耕種，甚得荒情。
value.en: He bought oxen and gave them to poor people so they could plow and plant, and greatly won the hearts of the famine-stricken.
value.literal: He bought oxen and gave them to poor people so they could plow and plant, and greatly won the hearts of the famine-stricken.

value.zh: 後除南中郎司馬、淮南太守。
value.en: Later he was appointed Sima of the Southern Gentlemen-of-the-Household and Administrator of Huainan.
value.literal: Later he was appointed Sima of the Southern Gentlemen-of-the-Household and Administrator of Huainan.

value.zh: 永明八年，巴東王子響殺僚佐，武帝召僧靜使領軍向江陵。
value.en: In the eighth year of Yongming, Prince Xiang of Badong murdered his officials. Emperor Wu ordered Dai Sengjing to take command and march on Jiangling.
value.literal: In the eighth year of Yongming, Prince Xiang of Badong killed his staff officers; Emperor Wu summoned Sengjing to lead the army toward Jiangling.

value.zh: 僧靜面啟上曰：「巴東王年少，長史司馬捉之太急，忿不思難故耳。
value.en: Dai Sengjing spoke plainly: "Prince Xiang of Badong is young. His chief administrator and staff supervisor seized him too roughly; in anger he struck without weighing the cost.
value.literal: Sengjing addressed the throne face to face, saying, "The Prince of Badong is young; the Chief Administrator and Staff Supervisor pressed him too hard, and in resentment he acted without thinking of the consequences.

value.zh: 天子兒過誤殺人，有何大罪，今急遣軍西上，人情惶懼，無所不至。
value.en: A son of the emperor who kills in a moment of passion—what capital crime is that? Dispatch an army west in haste and fear will spread everywhere.
value.literal: When a Son of Heaven's son kills someone in a passing error, what great crime is there? Now to rush troops westward will fill every heart with panic beyond measure.

value.zh: 臣不敢奉敕。」
value.en: I dare not obey this order."
value.literal: Your servant dares not accept the command."

value.zh: 上不答而心善之。
value.en: The emperor gave no reply yet was pleased in his heart.
value.literal: The emperor did not answer but inwardly approved of him.

value.zh: 徙廬陵王中軍司馬、高平太守。
value.en: He was moved to Staff Major to the Prince of Luling and Administrator of Gaoping.
value.literal: He was transferred to Staff Major to the Prince of Luling and Administrator of Gaoping.

value.zh: 卒，諡壯侯。
value.en: He died and received the posthumous title Marquis Zhuang.
value.literal: He died and was given the posthumous title Marquis Zhuang.

value.zh: 桓康，北蘭陵承人也。
value.en: Huan Kang came from Cheng in North Lanling.
value.literal: Huan Kang was a native of Cheng in North Lanling.

value.zh: 勇果驍悍。
value.en: He was courageous, fierce, and terrifying in battle.
value.literal: He was brave, resolute, fierce, and formidable.

value.zh: 宋大明中，隨齊高帝為軍容，從武帝在贛縣。
value.en: In Emperor Xiaoming's Daming reign he served Emperor Gao of Qi as army retainer and followed Emperor Wu at Gan County.
value.literal: During the Daming era of Song he followed Emperor Gao of Qi as army retainer and accompanied Emperor Wu at Gan County.

value.zh: 泰始初，武帝起義，為郡所縶，眾皆散。
value.en: When Emperor Wu first raised arms at the opening of Taishi, the commandery seized him and his followers scattered.
value.literal: At the beginning of Taishi, Emperor Wu raised the righteous army and was bound by the commandery; the crowd all scattered.

value.zh: 康裝擔，一頭貯穆後，一頭貯文惠太子及竟陵王子良，自負置山中。
value.en: Huan Kang shouldered two carrying-poles: one basket held Empress Mu, the other Crown Prince Wenhuai and Prince Ziliang of Jingling, and he bore them into the hills.
value.literal: Kang loaded two carrying-poles—one basket held Empress Mu, the other held Crown Prince Wenhuai and Prince Ziliang of Jingling—and bore them on his shoulders into the mountains.

value.zh: 及閘客蕭欣祖等四十餘人相結，破郡獄，出武帝。
value.en: He and over forty men, among them the gate guest Xiao Xingu, broke the jail and brought Emperor Wu out.
value.literal: Together with more than forty men including the gate guest Xiao Xingu, they joined forces, broke the commandery prison, and freed Emperor Wu.

value.zh: 郡追兵急，康等死戰破之。
value.en: Pursuit from the commandery was hot; Huan Kang and his band fought to the death and smashed through.
value.literal: The commandery pursuit was urgent; Kang and the others fought to the death and broke through.

value.zh: 隨武帝起兵，摧堅陷陣，膂力絕人。
value.en: He marched with Emperor Wu, tore through defenses, and possessed strength beyond any other man.
value.literal: Following Emperor Wu in raising troops, he stormed strongpoints and shattered formations; his physical strength was unmatched.

value.zh: 所經村邑，恣行暴害，江南人畏之，以其名怖小兒，畫其形於寺中。
value.en: Every hamlet he entered suffered his violence. Jiangnan feared him; parents painted his figure in temples to scare children.
value.literal: In every village he passed he committed outrages at will; the people of Jiangnan feared him and used his name to frighten small children, painting his likeness in temples.

value.zh: 病瘧者寫形帖著床壁，無不立愈。
value.en: Those with malaria who posted his portrait by the bed were said to recover at once.
value.literal: Malaria sufferers who copied his image and pasted it on the bed wall were all instantly cured.

value.zh: 建元元年，封吳平縣侯。
value.en: In the first year of Jianyuan he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuiping.
value.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan he was enfeoffed as Marquis of Wuiping County.

value.zh: 高帝謂康曰：「卿隨我日久，未得方伯，亦當未解我意，正欲與卿先共滅虜耳。」
value.en: Emperor Gao told him, "You have served me for years without a provincial post—you may still not grasp my meaning: I meant to crush the northern enemy with you first."
value.literal: Emperor Gao said to Kang, "You have followed me long without receiving a regional command—I suppose you still do not understand my intent; I simply wished first to destroy the barbarians together with you."

value.zh: 三年，魏軍動，康大破魏軍于淮陽。
value.en: the third year of In the Wei advanced; at Huaiyang Huan Kang routed them utterly.
value.literal: In the third year the Wei army moved; Kang inflicted a great defeat on the Wei army at Huaiyang.

value.zh: 武帝即位，卒于驍騎將軍。
value.en: After Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Huan Kang died in office as General of Valiant Cavalry.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, Kang died while General of Valiant Cavalry.

value.zh: 呂安國
value.en: Lu Anguo
value.literal: Lu Anguo

value.zh: 宋大明末，以將領見任，隱重有幹局，為劉勉所稱。
value.en: At the end of the Daming era of Song, Anguo was employed as a military commander. He was reserved, grave, capable, and organized, and was praised by Liu Mian.
value.literal: At the end of the Daming era of Song, Anguo was employed as a military commander; he was reserved, grave, capable, and organized, and was praised by Liu Mian.

value.zh: 泰始二年，為勉軍副，征殷琰，以功封鍾武縣男。
value.en: In the second year of Taishi, he served as deputy in Mian's army and campaigned against Yin Yan; for his merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Zhongwu County.
value.literal: In the second year of Taishi, he served as deputy in Mian's army and campaigned against Yin Yan; for his merit he was enfeoffed as Baron of Zhongwu County.

value.zh: 累遷兗州刺史。
value.en: He rose through successive promotions to Inspector of Yanzhou.
value.literal: He was repeatedly promoted, reaching Inspector of Yanzhou.

value.zh: 及沈攸之事起，齊高帝以安國為湘州刺史。
value.en: When Shen Youzhi rose in revolt, Emperor Gao of Qi made Anguo Inspector of Xiangzhou.
value.literal: When the affair of Shen Youzhi arose, Emperor Gao of Qi made Anguo Inspector of Xiangzhou.

value.zh: 建元元年，進爵為侯，轉右衛將軍，加給事中。
value.en: In the first year of Jianyuan (479), his title was advanced to marquis, he was transferred to General of the Right Guard, and the office of Palace Attendant was added.
value.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan, his title was advanced to marquis, he was transferred to General of the Right Guard, and the office of Palace Attendant was added.

value.zh: 後改封湘鄉侯。
value.en: Later his fief was changed to Marquis of Xiangxiang.
value.literal: Later his fief was changed to Marquis of Xiangxiang.

value.zh: 武帝即位，累遷光祿大夫，加散騎常侍。
value.en: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Anguo rose through successive promotions to Grandee of Splendid Happiness, with the added office of Cavalier Attendant.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Anguo was repeatedly promoted to Grandee of Splendid Happiness, with the added office of Cavalier Attendant.

value.zh: 齊高帝輔政，山圖密啟沈攸之久有異圖，宜為之備。
value.en: As regent, Emperor Gao of Qi received Shantu's secret report that Shen Youzhi had long plotted rebellion and must be watched.
value.literal: When Emperor Gao of Qi held the regency, Shantu secretly reported that Shen Youzhi had long harbored a different design and ought to be guarded against.

value.zh: 帝笑而納之。
value.en: The emperor smiled and took the warning to heart.
value.literal: The emperor smiled and accepted it.

value.zh: 攸之事起，武帝為西討都督，啟山圖為軍副。
value.en: When Youzhi rebelled, Emperor Wu commanded the western campaign and named Shantu his deputy.
value.literal: When Youzhi's affair arose, Emperor Wu was Western Campaign Commander-in-Chief and requested Shantu as army deputy.

value.zh: 攸之攻郢城，武帝令山圖量其形勢。
value.en: Youzhi besieged Ying; Emperor Wu asked Shantu to read the field.
value.literal: Youzhi attacked Ying City; Emperor Wu ordered Shantu to assess the situation.

value.zh: 山圖曰：「攸之為人，性度險刻，無以結固士心。
value.en: Shantu said, "Youzhi is harsh by nature and cannot bind his officers' loyalty.
value.literal: Shantu said, "Youzhi as a man is by nature harsh and cutting and cannot firmly bind the hearts of his officers.

value.zh: 如頓兵堅城之下，適所以為離散之漸耳。」
value.en: Pin him under a strong wall and his host will melt away."
value.literal: If he camps his host under a strong city, that will only hasten their scattering."

value.zh: 及攸之敗，高帝謂曰：「周公前言，可謂明於見事矣。」
value.en: After Youzhi's fall, Emperor Gao said, "Your forecast showed true foresight."
value.literal: When Youzhi was defeated, Emperor Gao said, "Your earlier words can be called clear-sighted in reading events."

value.zh: 建元元年，封晉興縣男。
value.en: In the first year of Jianyuan (479), Shantu was enfeoffed as Baron of Jinxing County.
value.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan, Shantu was enfeoffed as Baron of Jinxing County.

value.zh: 武帝踐阼，遷竟陵王鎮北司馬，帶南平昌太守。
value.en: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Shantu was transferred to Sima of the Prince of Jingling's Army That Guards the North and concurrently Administrator of Southern Pingchang.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, Shantu was transferred to Sima of the Prince of Jingling's Army That Guards the North and concurrently Administrator of Southern Pingchang.

value.zh: 以盆城之舊，出入殿省，甚見親信。
value.en: Because of their old association at Pencheng, he entered and exited the palace offices and was deeply trusted.
value.literal: Because of their old association at Pencheng, he entered and exited the palace offices and was deeply trusted.

value.zh: 義鄉縣長風廟神姓鄧，先經為縣令，死遂發靈，山圖啟乞加神位輔國將軍。
value.en: The spirit of Changfeng Shrine in Yixiang County had the surname Deng. He had once served as county magistrate, and after death manifested numinous power, so Shantu requested that the spirit's rank be increased to General Who Assists the State.
value.literal: The spirit of Changfeng Shrine in Yixiang County had the surname Deng; he had once served as county magistrate, and after death manifested numinous power, so Shantu submitted a request that the spirit's rank be increased to General Who Assists the State.

value.zh: 上答曰：「足狗肉便了事，何用階級為。」
value.en: The emperor replied, "Enough dog meat will settle the matter; what use is rank?"
value.literal: The emperor replied, "Enough dog meat will settle the matter; what use is rank?"

value.zh: 永明五年，為大司馬，加征虜將軍、濟陽太守。
value.en: In the fifth year of Yongming he became Grand Marshal, with added rank as General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Administrator of Jiyang.
value.literal: In the fifth year of Yongming he was made Grand Marshal, with the additional titles General Who Subdues the Barbarians and Administrator of Jiyang.

value.zh: 武帝數講武，嘗令盤龍領馬軍，校騎騁矟。
value.en: The emperor often held war games and had Panlong lead the horse corps in spear drills.
value.literal: Emperor Wu often held martial lectures and would have Panlong lead the cavalry, comparing horses in spear charges.

value.zh: 後以疾，為光祿大夫。
value.en: Illness later made him Grand Master of the Palace.
value.literal: Later because of illness he was made Grand Master of the Palace.

value.zh: 還為散騎常侍、光祿大夫。
value.en: He returned as Regular Attendant and Grand Master of the Palace.
value.literal: On return he was made Regular Attendant and Grand Master of the Palace.

value.zh: 武帝戲之曰：「卿著貂蟬，何如兜鍪？」
value.en: The emperor teased him: "You wear court finery—how is that like a helm?"
value.literal: Emperor Wu jested with him, saying, "You wear the cicada and fur finial—how does that compare to a helmet?"

value.zh: 盤龍曰：「此貂蟬從兜鍪中生耳。」
value.en: Panlong answered, "This finery grew out of the helmet."
value.literal: Panlong said, "This finery was born from the helmet."

value.zh: 尋病卒，年七十九。
value.en: He soon died of illness, aged seventy-nine.
value.literal: Soon he died of illness at age seventy-nine.

value.zh: 子奉叔，勇力絕人，少隨盤龍征討，所在暴掠。
value.en: His son Fengshu possessed matchless strength. From youth he campaigned with Panlong and looted wherever he marched.
value.literal: His son Fengshu had strength surpassing others; from youth he followed Panlong on campaigns and wherever he went he plundered violently.

value.zh: 為東宮直合將軍。
value.en: He became Direct Guard General of the Eastern Palace.
value.literal: He was Direct Guard General of the Eastern Palace.

value.zh: 郁林在西州，奉叔密得自進，及即位，與直合將軍曹道剛為心膂。
value.en: While Yulin was heir in the Western Quarter, Fengshu found private access to him. On Yulin's accession he and Cao Daogang became the emperor's inner circle.
value.literal: When Yulin was in the Western Quarter, Fengshu secretly gained access to present himself; when Yulin took the throne he and Direct Guard General Cao Daogang became his inner confidants.

value.zh: 奉叔善騎馬，帝從其學騎，尤見親寵，得入內，無所忌憚。
value.en: Fengshu rode superbly; the emperor learned horsemanship from him and favored him so that he entered the inner palace without restraint.
value.literal: Fengshu was skilled at riding horses; the emperor learned riding from him and favored him especially, gaining entry within the palace without restraint or fear.

value.zh: 陵轢朝士，就司空王敬則換米二百斛，敬則以百斛與之，不受。
value.en: He bullied officials. Demanding two hundred piculs of grain from Wang Jingze, he refused the hundred piculs offered.
value.literal: He bullied court gentlemen; he went to Minister of Works Wang Jingze to exchange for two hundred piculs of grain; Jingze gave him one hundred piculs and he would not accept it.

value.zh: 敬則大懼，乃更餉二百斛並金鉿等物。
value.en: Terrified, Jingze sent another two hundred piculs plus gold hairpins and gifts.
value.literal: Jingze was greatly afraid and therefore sent another two hundred piculs together with gold hairpins and other objects.

value.zh: 敬則有一內妓，帝令奉叔求。
value.en: Jingze kept a palace woman; the emperor ordered Fengshu to take her.
value.literal: Jingze had a palace concubine; the emperor ordered Fengshu to demand her.

value.zh: 奉叔不通徑前，從者執單刀皆半拔，敬則跣走入內。
value.en: Fengshu stormed in without ceremony, followers' blades half drawn. Jingze fled barefoot indoors.
value.literal: Fengshu would not go by the proper path; his followers drew single blades half unsheathed; Jingze ran in barefoot into the inner quarters.

value.zh: 既而自計不免，乃出，遙呼奉叔曰：「弟那忽能顧？」
value.en: Seeing escape impossible, he came out and called, "Brother, how can you treat me so?"
value.literal: Then calculating he could not escape, he came out and called from afar to Fengshu, "Younger brother, how could you suddenly turn on me?"

value.zh: 奉叔宣旨求妓意，乃得釋。
value.en: Fengshu stated the imperial demand for the woman, and Jingze was spared.
value.literal: Fengshu announced the imperial intent seeking the concubine, and only then was he released.

value.zh: 與綦母珍、曹道剛、朱隆之共相唇齒，煽弄威權。
value.en: With Qi Mu Zhen, Cao Daogang, and Zhu Longzhi he formed a clique that twisted power at will.
value.literal: With Qi Mu Zhen, Cao Daogang, and Zhu Longzhi they were like lips and teeth, fanning and wielding authority.

value.zh: 奉叔常翼單刀二十口，出入禁闈，既無別詔，門衛莫敢訶。
value.en: He routinely carried twenty swords through the forbidden gates; without a special edict guards dared not stop him.
value.literal: Fengshu commonly carried twenty single blades at his side entering and leaving the forbidden gates; as there was no separate edict, the gate guards dared not challenge him.

value.zh: 每語人云：「周郎刀不識君。」
value.en: He would say, "Young Zhou's blade knows no master but me."
value.literal: He often told people, "Young Zhou's blade does not know you."

value.zh: 求武帝御角及輿，並求禦仗以給左右。
value.en: He demanded the emperor's horn bow, carriage, and imperial arms for his men.
value.literal: He sought the emperor's horn bow and carriage and also sought imperial arms to supply his attendants.

value.zh: 事無不從。
value.en: Nothing was refused.
value.literal: In affairs nothing was refused him.

value.zh: 又求黃門郎，明帝作輔，固執不能得，乃令蕭諶、蕭坦之說帝出奉叔為外鎮，樹腹心。
value.en: He sought Palace Attendant rank; regent Emperor Ming refused. Xiao Chen and Xiao Tanzhi then persuaded the emperor to post Fengshu abroad and plant a loyal man within.
value.literal: He also sought the post of Palace Attendant; when Emperor Ming was regent he firmly would not grant it; then he had Xiao Chen and Xiao Tanzhi persuade the emperor to send Fengshu out to a frontier command and plant a trusted man in his place.

value.zh: 又說奉叔以方伯之重，奉叔納其言。
value.en: They flattered him with a provincial command; he agreed.
value.literal: They also persuaded Fengshu with the weight of a regional command; Fengshu accepted their words.

value.zh: 隆昌元年，出為青、冀二州刺史。
value.en: In the first year of Longchang he was sent out as Inspector of Qing and Ji.
value.literal: In the first year of Longchang he went out as Inspector of Qing and Ji provinces.

value.zh: 奉叔就帝求千戶侯，帝許之。
value.en: He asked the throne for a thousand-household marquisate; the emperor agreed.
value.literal: Fengshu asked the emperor for a marquisate of one thousand households; the emperor consented.

value.zh: 明帝以為不可。
value.en: Emperor Ming objected.
value.literal: Emperor Ming thought it could not be done.

value.zh: 忽謂蕭諶曰：「若不能見與千戶侯，不復應減五百戶；
value.en: He told Xiao Chen sharply, "Deny me a thousand-household marquis and I will not take five hundred less either;
value.literal: Suddenly he said to Xiao Chen, "If you cannot give me a thousand-household marquisate, I will not accept even five hundred households being reduced;

value.zh: 不爾，周郎當就刀頭取辦耳。」
value.en: or Young Zhou will settle it at sword point."
value.literal: otherwise Young Zhou will settle the matter at the blade's point."

value.zh: 既而封曲江縣男，奉叔大怒，於眾中攘刀，厲目切齒。
value.en: He was given only Viscount of Qujiang. Fengshu raged, drew his blade in the assembly, glaring and gnashing his teeth.
value.literal: Soon he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Qujiang; Fengshu was furious and in the crowd brandished his blade, glaring and grinding his teeth.

value.zh: 明帝說諭乃受。
value.en: Emperor Ming talked him down before he accepted.
value.literal: Emperor Ming persuaded and instructed him and only then did he accept.

value.zh: 及將之鎮，明帝慮其不可復製，因其早入，引往後堂，執送廷尉盡之。
value.en: Before he could depart, Emperor Ming feared losing control. Lured early to the rear hall, he was seized and executed to the last man at court.
value.literal: When he was about to go to his command, Emperor Ming feared he could not be controlled again; because he entered early, he was led to the rear hall, seized, and sent to the Minister of Justice, where he was executed to the last man.

value.zh: 王廣之字士林，一字林之，沛郡相人也。
value.en: Wang Guangzhi, courtesy names Shilin and Linzhi, came from Xiang in Pei commandery.
value.literal: Wang Guangzhi, style Shilin, also styled Linzhi, was a native of Xiang in Pei commandery.

value.zh: 少好弓馬，便捷有勇力。
value.en: From youth he loved bow and horse, was quick, brave, and strong.
value.literal: From youth he loved bow and horse; he was nimble and possessed courage and strength.

value.zh: 初為馬隊主，隨劉勉征殷琰。
value.en: He began as horse detachment chief under Liu Mian against Yin Yan.
value.literal: At first he was chief of a horse detachment and followed Liu Mian in campaigning against Yin Yan.

value.zh: 兵既盛而合肥戍又阻兵為寇。
value.en: The army was strong, but the Hefei garrison also blocked them as enemies.
value.literal: The army was already strong yet the Hefei garrison also blocked the army as bandits.

value.zh: 勉宣令軍中求征合肥者，以大郡賞之。
value.en: Mian called for volunteers to take Hefei, promising a great commandery as prize.
value.literal: Mian proclaimed throughout the army seeking one to campaign against Hefei, with a great commandery as reward.

value.zh: 廣之曰：「若得將軍所乘馬，判能制之。」
value.en: Guangzhi said, "Give me the general's own horse and I will take it."
value.literal: Guangzhi said, "If I obtain the general's own mount, I can surely subdue it."

value.zh: 勉幢主皇甫肅謂勉曰：「廣之敢奪節下馬，可斬。」
value.en: Mian's banner chief Huangfu Su said, "Guangzhi dares seize your horse—cut him down."
value.literal: Mian's banner chief Huangfu Su said to Mian, "Guangzhi dares seize my lord's horse—he should be beheaded."

value.zh: 勉曰：「觀其意必能立功。」
value.en: Mian said, "He means to win glory—let him try."
value.literal: Mian said, "Judging his intent he will surely be able to achieve merit."

value.zh: 即推鞍下馬與之。
value.en: He dismounted and gave him the horse.
value.literal: He immediately pushed off the saddle and dismounted, giving the horse to him.

value.zh: 及行，合肥果拔，勉大賞之，即擢為軍主。
value.en: Hefei fell. Mian richly rewarded him and made him army commander at once.
value.literal: When they marched, Hefei was indeed taken; Mian greatly rewarded him and immediately promoted him to army commander.

value.zh: 廣之於勉前謂肅曰：「節下若從卿言，非唯斬壯士，亦自無以平賊。
value.en: Before Mian, Guangzhi told Su, "Had your lord listened to you, he would have killed a hero and never pacified the enemy.
value.literal: Before Mian, Guangzhi said to Su, "If my lord had followed your advice, he would not only have beheaded a stalwart but also himself have had no means to pacify the bandits.

value.zh: 卿不賞才乃至此邪！」
value.en: You cannot recognize talent—that is your fault!"
value.literal: You do not reward talent and have come to this!"

value.zh: 廣之由此知名。
value.en: From this Guangzhi became famous.
value.literal: Guangzhi thereby became renowned.

value.zh: 初封蒲圻子。
value.en: He was first enfeoffed Viscount of Puqi.
value.literal: At first he was enfeoffed as Viscount of Puqi.

value.zh: 肅有學術，善舉止，廣之亦雅相推慕。
value.en: Su was learned and graceful; Guangzhi admired him sincerely.
value.literal: Su had learning and fine deportment; Guangzhi also in refined fashion admired and looked up to him.

value.zh: 勉亡後，肅更依廣之，廣之盛相賞接，啟武帝以為東海太守，不念舊惡如此。
value.en: After Mian's death Su clung to Guangzhi, who favored him and recommended him to Emperor Wu as Administrator of Donghai—forgetting old quarrels.
value.literal: After Mian died, Su again relied on Guangzhi; Guangzhi greatly favored and received him and reported to Emperor Wu to make him Administrator of Donghai—so little did he bear old grudges.

value.zh: 廣之後以征伐功，位給事中、冠軍將軍，改封寧都縣子。
value.en: For campaigns he became Gentleman of the Palace and General Who Vanquishes Champions, re-enfeoffed Viscount of Ningdu.
value.literal: Later Guangzhi for campaign merit held the post of Gentleman of the Palace and General Who Vanquishes Champions and his enfeoffment was changed to Viscount of Ningdu.

value.zh: 齊高帝廢蒼梧，出廣之為徐州刺史、鍾離太守。
value.en: When Emperor Gao deposed the Cangwu emperor, Guangzhi was sent as Inspector of Xu and Administrator of Zhongli.
value.literal: When Emperor Gao of Qi deposed the Cangwu emperor, he sent Guangzhi out as Inspector of Xu Province and Administrator of Zhongli.

value.zh: 沈攸之事起，廣之留都下，豫平石頭，仍從高帝頓新亭。
value.en: When Shen Youzhi rebelled, Guangzhi stayed in the capital, helped take Stone City, and followed Emperor Gao to Xinting.
value.literal: When Shen Youzhi's affair arose, Guangzhi remained in the capital, took part in pacifying Stone City, and still followed Emperor Gao to encamp at Xinting.

value.zh: 高帝誅黃回，回弟駟及從弟馬、兄子奴亡逸。
value.en: When Huang Hui was executed, his brother Si, cousin Ma, and nephew Nu fled.
value.literal: When Emperor Gao executed Huang Hui, Hui's younger brother Si and cousin Ma and elder brother's son Nu fled and vanished.

value.zh: 高帝與廣之書曰：「黃回雖有微勳，而罪過轉不可容。
value.en: Emperor Gao wrote Guangzhi: "Huang Hui's small merits could not balance his crimes.
value.literal: Emperor Gao wrote to Guangzhi, "Huang Hui though he had slight merit, his crimes in the end could not be tolerated.

value.zh: 近遂啟請禦大小二輿為刺史服飾，吾乃不惜為其啟聞，政恐得輿復求畫輪車。
value.en: He lately asked for imperial carriages fit for an inspector; I would have reported it, fearing he would next demand a painted imperial coach.
value.literal: Recently he even requested the great and small imperial carriages for inspector's regalia; I was not unwilling to report it for him, but only feared that obtaining the carriage he would again request a painted-wheel carriage.

value.zh: 此外罪不可勝數，弟自悉之。
value.en: His other crimes are countless—you know them.
value.literal: Beyond this his crimes are beyond counting—you yourself know them.

value.zh: 今啟依法。」
value.en: Execute the law now."
value.literal: Now I report according to law."

value.zh: 令廣之於江西搜捕駟等。
value.en: He ordered Guangzhi to hunt Si and the rest west of the Yangzi.
value.literal: He ordered Guangzhi to search west of the river and capture Si and the others.

value.zh: 建元元年，進爵為侯。
value.en: In the first year of Jianyuan (479), Guangzhi's title was advanced to marquis.
value.literal: In the first year of Jianyuan, Guangzhi's title was advanced to marquis.

value.zh: 武帝即位，累遷右衛將軍，散騎常侍，前軍將軍。
value.en: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, he rose through successive promotions to General of the Right Guard, Cavalier Attendant, and General of the Van.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu ascended the throne, he was repeatedly promoted to General of the Right Guard, Cavalier Attendant, and General of the Van.

value.zh: 延興元年，為豫州刺史，豫廢郁林。
value.en: In the first year of Yanxing, he became Inspector of Yuzhou and took part in deposing Yulin.
value.literal: In the first year of Yanxing, he became Inspector of Yuzhou and took part in deposing Yulin.

value.zh: 後拜鎮南將軍、江州刺史，進應城縣公。
value.en: Later he was appointed General Who Guards the South and Inspector of Jiangzhou, and his title was advanced to Duke of Yingcheng County.
value.literal: Later he was appointed General Who Guards the South and Inspector of Jiangzhou, and his title was advanced to Duke of Yingcheng County.

value.zh: 建武中，位侍中、鎮軍將軍，給扶。
value.en: During Jianwu, he held the offices of Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Guards the Army and was granted an armrest.
value.literal: During Jianwu, he held the offices of Attendant-in-Ordinary and General Who Guards the Army and was granted an armrest.

value.zh: 後卒，贈車騎將軍，諡壯公。
value.en: Later he died, was posthumously given the office of General of Chariots and Cavalry, and received the posthumous title Duke Zhuang.
value.literal: Later he died, was posthumously given the office of General of Chariots and Cavalry, and received the posthumous title Duke Zhuang.

value.zh: 永明初，遷桂陽內史，討捕賊盜，境內肅清。
value.en: Early in Yongming he governed Guiyang, crushed bandits, and cleared the region.
value.literal: At the beginning of Yongming he was transferred to Interior Administrator of Guiyang, pursued and captured bandits and robbers, and within the borders was cleared and pacified.

value.zh: 罷任還都，路經江州，刺史柳世隆臨渚餞別，見珍國還裝輕素，歎曰：「此真良二千石也，」還為大司馬中兵參軍。
value.en: Returning to court via Jiang Province, Liu Shilong saw his light baggage and sighed, "A true two-thousand-dan official," then named him Major under the Grand Marshal.
value.literal: Leaving office and returning to the capital, his route passed Jiang Province; Inspector Liu Shilong came to the ford to bid farewell; seeing Zhenguo's return baggage light and plain, he sighed and said, "This is truly a good two-thousand-dan official," and on return he was made Major in the Grand Marshal's central army.

value.zh: 武帝雅相知賞，謂其父廣之曰：「珍國應堪大用，卿可謂老蚌也。」
value.en: Emperor Wu prized him and told Guangzhi, "Zhenguo deserves high office—you are the old oyster that bore the pearl."
value.literal: Emperor Wu in refined fashion knew and appreciated him and said to his father Guangzhi, "Zhenguo should be fit for great employment—you may be called an old oyster."

value.zh: 廣之曰：「臣不敢辭。」
value.en: Guangzhi said, "I dare not refuse the praise."
value.literal: Guangzhi said, "Your servant dares not decline."

value.zh: 帝大笑。
value.en: The emperor laughed aloud.
value.literal: The emperor laughed greatly.

value.zh: 帝每歎曰：「晚代將家子弟如珍國者少矣。」
value.en: He often said, "Few sons of generals in this age match Zhenguo."
value.literal: The emperor often sighed, "In this late age there are few sons of general's houses like Zhenguo."

value.zh: 累遷遊擊將軍，父憂去職。
value.en: He rose to General Who Roams in Attack, then left for mourning his father.
value.literal: He was repeatedly promoted to General Who Roams in Attack and left office for his father's mourning.

value.zh: 戴法興 徐爰 阮佃夫 紀僧真 劉系宗 茹法亮 呂文顯 茹法珍 周石珍 陸驗 司馬申 施文慶 沈客卿 孔範
value.en: Dai Faxing, Xu Ai, Ruan Dianfu, Ji Sengzhen, Liu Xizong, Ru Faliang, Lü Wenxian, Ru Fazhen, Zhou Shizhen, Lu Yan, Sima Shen, Shi Wenqing, Shen Keqing, and Kong Fan
value.literal: Dai Faxing, Xu Ai, Ruan Dianfu, Ji Sengzhen, Liu Xizong, Ru Faliang, Lü Wenxian, Ru Fazhen, Zhou Shizhen, Lu Yan, Sima Shen, Shi Wenqing, Shen Keqing, and Kong Fan

value.zh: 系宗久在朝省，閑於職事，武帝常云：「學士輩不堪經國，唯大讀書耳。
value.en: Xizong had long served in court offices and was adept at administrative work. Emperor Wu often said, "These scholar-officials cannot govern the state—they merely read books at great length.
value.literal: Xizong had long served in court offices and was adept at administrative affairs. Emperor Wu often said, "These scholar-officials cannot manage the state—they merely read books extensively.

value.zh: 經國，一劉系宗足矣。
value.en: For governing the state, one Liu Xizong is enough.
value.literal: For governing the state, one Liu Xizong is enough.

value.zh: 沈約、王融數百人，于事何用。」
value.en: Of what use are Shen Yue, Wang Rong, and their hundreds for practical affairs?"
value.literal: Of what use are Shen Yue, Wang Rong, and their hundreds for practical matters?"

value.zh: 其重吏事如此。
value.en: Such was the weight he placed on practical administration.
value.literal: Such was the weight he placed on practical administration.

value.zh: 建武二年，卒官。
value.en: In the second year of Jianwu he died in office.
value.literal: In the second year of Jianwu he died in office.

value.zh: 茹法亮，吳興武康人也。
value.en: Ru Faliang was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.
value.literal: Ru Faliang was a native of Wukang in Wuxing.

value.zh: 宋大明中，出身為小史。
value.en: During the Daming era of Emperor Ming of Song he began his career as a petty clerk.
value.literal: During Emperor Ming of Song's Daming era he began his career as a petty clerk.

value.zh: 曆齋幹扶侍。
value.en: He served in turn as orderly in the fast hall and as attendant.
value.literal: He served successively as orderly in the fast hall and as attendant.

value.zh: 孝武末年，鞭罰過度，校獵江右，選白衣左右百八十人，皆面首富室，從至南州，得鞭者過半。
value.en: Near the end of Emperor Xiaowu of Song's reign, floggings were excessive. During a hunting expedition on the right bank of the Yangtze, one hundred eighty attendants in plain dress were selected—all wealthy men from prominent households. They accompanied him to the southern regions, and more than half were flogged.
value.literal: Near the end of Emperor Xiaowu of Song's reign, floggings were excessive. During a hunting expedition on the right bank of the Yangtze, one hundred eighty attendants in plain dress were selected—all were wealthy men of prominent households. They accompanied him to the southern regions, and more than half received floggings.

value.zh: 法亮憂懼，因緣啟出家得為道人。
value.en: Anxious and afraid, Faliang seized an opportunity to petition to leave home and become a Daoist monk.
value.literal: Faliang, anxious and afraid, seized an opportunity to petition to leave home and become a Daoist monk.

value.zh: 明帝初，罷道，結事阮佃夫，累至齊高帝冠軍府行參軍。
value.en: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign he left the monastic life, attached himself to Ruan Dianfu, and rose to Acting Staff Officer in Emperor Gao of Qi's Champion General headquarters.
value.literal: At the beginning of Emperor Ming's reign he left the monastic life, attached himself to Ruan Dianfu, and rose to Acting Staff Officer in Emperor Gao of Qi's Champion General headquarters.

value.zh: 及武帝鎮盆城，須舊驅使人，法亮求留為武帝江州典簽，除南台御史，帶松滋令。
value.en: When Emperor Wu was garrisoned at Pencheng and needed his old runners and attendants, Faliang asked to remain as Chief Clerk of Jiangzhou for the future emperor. He was appointed Censor of the Southern Office and concurrent magistrate of Songzi.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu was garrisoned at Pencheng and needed his old runners and attendants, Faliang asked to remain as Chief Clerk of Jiangzhou for the future emperor; he was appointed Censor of the Southern Office and concurrent Magistrate of Songzi.

value.zh: 法亮便僻解事，善於承奉，稍見委信。
value.en: Faliang was quick-witted and capable, skilled at flattery and service, and gradually won trust.
value.literal: Faliang was quick-witted and capable, skilled at flattery and service, and gradually won trust.

value.zh: 建元初，度東宮主書，除奉朝請，補東宮通事舍人。
value.en: At the beginning of Jianyuan he transferred to serve as chief secretary in the Eastern Palace, was made Court Gentleman, and appointed Confidential Messenger in the Eastern Palace.
value.literal: At the beginning of Jianyuan he crossed over to serve as chief secretary in the Eastern Palace, was made Court Gentleman, and appointed Confidential Messenger in the Eastern Palace.

value.zh: 武帝即位，仍為中書通事舍人，除員外郎，帶南濟陰太守。
value.en: When Emperor Wu took the throne, he remained Confidential Messenger of the Central Secretariat, was appointed Supernumerary Gentleman, and served concurrently as administrator of South Jiyin.
value.literal: When Emperor Wu took the throne, he remained Confidential Messenger of the Central Secretariat, was appointed Supernumerary Gentleman, and served concurrently as Administrator of South Jiyin.

value.zh: 與會稽呂文度、臨海呂文顯並以奸佞諂事武帝。
value.en: Together with Lü Wendu of Kuaiji and Lü Wenxian of Linhai, he relied on sycophancy and deceit to serve Emperor Wu.
value.literal: Together with Lü Wendu of Kuaiji and Lü Wenxian of Linhai, he relied on sycophancy and deceit to serve Emperor Wu.

value.zh: 文度為外監，專制兵權，領軍將軍守虛位而已。
value.en: Wendu served as Outer Supervisor with monopolistic control of military authority, while the General of the Guards held nothing but an empty title.
value.literal: Wendu served as Outer Supervisor with monopolistic control of military authority; the General of the Guards held nothing but an empty title.

value.zh: 天文寺常以上將星占文度吉凶。
value.en: The Astronomical Bureau regularly used the general's star to read Wendu's fortune.
value.literal: The Astronomical Bureau regularly used the general's star to read Wendu's fortune.

value.zh: 文度尤見委信，上嘗云：「公卿中有憂國如文度者，復何憂天下不寧。」
value.en: Wendu was especially trusted. The emperor once said, "If among the ministers and nobles there were one who cared for the state as Wendu does, what worry would there be that the realm would not be at peace?"
value.literal: Wendu was especially trusted. The emperor once said, "If among the ministers and nobles there were one who cared for the state as Wendu does, what worry would there be that the realm would not be at peace?"

value.zh: 巴東王子響于荊州殺僚佐，上遣軍西上，使法亮宣旨安撫子響。
value.en: Prince Zixiang of Badong killed his staff officers in Jingzhou. The emperor dispatched troops westward and sent Faliang to proclaim the imperial will and pacify him.
value.literal: Prince Zixiang of Badong killed his staff officers in Jingzhou; the emperor dispatched troops westward and sent Faliang to proclaim the imperial will and pacify Zixiang.

value.zh: 法亮至江津，子響呼法亮，疑畏不肯往。
value.en: When Faliang reached Jiangjin, Zixiang summoned him, but Faliang, suspicious and afraid, refused to go.
value.literal: When Faliang reached Jiangjin, Zixiang summoned him, but Faliang, suspicious and afraid, refused to go.

value.zh: 又求見傳詔，法亮又不遣。
value.en: Zixiang also asked to see the edict-bearer, and Faliang again refused to send him.
value.literal: Zixiang also requested to see the edict-bearer, and Faliang again would not send him.

value.zh: 故子響怒，遣兵破尹略軍。
value.en: Zixiang thereupon grew angry and sent troops to crush Yin Lue's army.
value.literal: Thereupon Zixiang grew angry and sent troops to crush Yin Lue's army.

value.zh: 事平，法亮至江陵，誅賞處分，皆稱敕斷決。
value.en: Once the affair was settled, Faliang went to Jiangling. Executions, rewards, and dispositions were all said to have been decided by imperial edict.
value.literal: When the affair was settled, Faliang went to Jiangling; executions, rewards, and dispositions all were said to have been decided by imperial edict.

value.zh: 軍還，上悔誅子響，法亮被責，少時親任如舊。
value.en: When the army returned, the emperor regretted executing Zixiang. Faliang was rebuked, but before long he enjoyed the emperor's intimate trust as before.
value.literal: When the army returned, the emperor regretted executing Zixiang; Faliang was rebuked, but before long he was trusted as intimately as before.

value.zh: 廣開宅宇，杉齋光麗，與延昌殿相埒。
value.en: He greatly expanded his residence. His cedar hall was bright and splendid, rivaling the Yanchang Hall.
value.literal: He greatly expanded his residence; his cedar hall was bright and splendid, matching the Yanchang Hall.

value.zh: 延昌殿，武帝中齋也。
value.en: Yanchang Hall was Emperor Wu's inner fast hall.
value.literal: Yanchang Hall was Emperor Wu's inner fast hall.

value.zh: 宅後為魚池釣台，土山樓館，長廊將一里。
value.en: Behind the residence lay a fish pond and angling terrace, earthen hills with pavilions, and a corridor nearly a li in length.
value.literal: Behind the residence were a fish pond and angling terrace, earthen hills with pavilions, and a corridor nearly a li long.

value.zh: 竹林花藥之美，公家苑囿所不能及。
value.en: The beauty of its bamboo groves, flowers, and medicinal plants surpassed even the imperial gardens.
value.literal: The beauty of its bamboo groves, flowers, and herbs surpassed what the palace gardens could match.

value.zh: 郁林即位，除步兵校尉。
value.en: When Emperor Yulin ascended the throne, Faliang was appointed commandant of footsoldiers.
value.literal: When Emperor Yulin ascended the throne, Faliang was appointed Commandant of Footsoldiers.

value.zh: 時有綦母珍之，居舍人之任，凡所論薦，事無不允。
value.en: At this time Qimu Zhenzhi held the post of attendant, and whatever nominations he put forward were invariably approved.
value.literal: At this time there was Qimu Zhenzhi, who held the post of attendant; whatever nominations he put forward were invariably approved.

value.zh: 內外要職及郡丞尉，皆論價而後施行。
value.en: Important posts inside and outside the court, as well as county assistant magistrates and commandants, were all sold by negotiated price before appointment.
value.literal: Important posts inside and outside the court, as well as county assistant magistrates and commandants, all were sold by negotiated price before appointment.

value.zh: 貨賄交至，旬月之間，累至千金。
value.en: Bribes poured in without cease, and within a month or so they accumulated to a thousand gold pieces.
value.literal: Bribes flowed in without cease; within a month or so they accumulated to a thousand gold pieces.

value.zh: 帝給珍之宅，宅邊又有空宅，從即並取，輒令材官營作，不關詔旨。
value.en: The emperor granted Zhenzhi a residence. There was another empty residence beside it, which he seized on the spot as well, then ordered the construction officer to build there without any imperial edict.
value.literal: The emperor granted Zhenzhi a residence; there was another empty residence beside it, which he took on the spot as well, then ordered the construction officer to build there without reference to an edict.

value.zh: 材官將軍細作丞相語云：「寧拒至尊敕，不可違舍人命。」
value.en: The construction officer general wittily echoed the prime minister's words: "Better to refuse the supreme sovereign's edict than to disobey an attendant's order."
value.literal: The construction officer general finely mimicked the prime minister's speech, saying, "Better to refuse the supreme sovereign's edict than to disobey an attendant's order."

value.zh: 珍之母隨弟欽之作暨陽令，欽之罷縣還，珍之迎母至湖熟，輒將青氅百人自隨，鼓角橫吹，都下富人追從者百數。
value.en: Zhenzhi's mother had accompanied his younger brother Qinzhi when the latter served as magistrate of Jiyang. When Qinzhi left office and returned, Zhenzhi went to meet his mother at Hushu with a hundred green-cloaked guards, drums, horns, and wind instruments playing, and scores of wealthy men of the capital followed in his train.
value.literal: Zhenzhi's mother followed his younger brother Qinzhi when the latter served as magistrate of Jiyang; when Qinzhi left office and returned, Zhenzhi went to meet his mother at Hushu, bringing with him a hundred green-cloaked guards, with drums, horns, and wind instruments playing; wealthy men of the capital followed in scores.

value.zh: 欽之自行佐作縣，還除廬陵王驃騎正將軍，又詐宣敕使欽之領青氅。
value.en: Qinzhi had himself served as assistant magistrate in the county. On his return he was appointed regular general under the Prince of Luling's fast cavalry headquarters, and Zhenzhi also falsely proclaimed an edict appointing Qinzhi to command the green-cloaked guards.
value.literal: Qinzhi had himself served as assistant magistrate in the county; on his return he was appointed Regular General under the Fast Cavalry headquarters of the Prince of Luling, and Zhenzhi also falsely proclaimed an edict appointing Qinzhi to command the green-cloaked guards.

value.zh: 珍之有一銅鏡，背有「三公」字，常語人云：「征祥如此，何患三公不至。」
value.en: Zhenzhi owned a bronze mirror with the characters "Three Dukes" on the back. He often told people, "With such an omen, why worry that the rank of Three Dukes will not come?"
value.literal: Zhenzhi had a bronze mirror with the characters "Three Dukes" on the back; he often told people, "With such an omen, why worry that the rank of Three Dukes will not come?"

value.zh: 乃就蔣王廟乞願得三公，封郡王。
value.en: He went to the Temple of Prince Jiang to pray that he might attain the Three Dukes and be enfeoffed as a commandery prince.
value.literal: He went to the Temple of Prince Jiang to pray for attainment of the Three Dukes and enfeoffment as a commandery prince.

value.zh: 啟帝求封，朝議未許。
value.en: He petitioned the emperor for enfeoffment, but the court deliberation did not approve.
value.literal: He petitioned the emperor for enfeoffment, but court deliberation did not approve.

value.zh: 又自陳曰：「珍之西州伏事，侍從入宮，契闊心膂，竭盡誠力。
value.en: He also declared in person, "Zhenzhi served humbly in the Western Province, followed the emperor into the palace, shared hardships heart and soul, and exhausted my loyalty and strength.
value.literal: He also declared in his own person, "Zhenzhi served humbly in the Western Province, followed into the palace, shared hardships heart and soul, and exhausted my loyalty and strength.

value.zh: 王融奸謀潛構，自非珍之翼衛扶持，事在不測。
value.en: Wang Rong secretly plotted treachery. Had it not been for Zhenzhi's protection and support, the outcome would have been unpredictable.
value.literal: Wang Rong secretly plotted treachery; had it not been for Zhenzhi's protection and support, the outcome would have been unpredictable.

value.zh: 今惜千戶侯，誰為官使者。」
value.en: If you begrudge me now a marquisate of a thousand households, who will serve as your agent at court?"
value.literal: Now if you begrudge me a marquisate of a thousand households, who will serve as your agent at court?"

value.zh: 又有牒自論於朝廷曰：「當世祖晏駕之時，內外紛擾，珍之手抱至尊，口行處分，忠誠契闊，人誰不知。
value.en: He also submitted a memorial arguing before the court, "When Emperor Shizu passed away, turmoil reigned within and without. Zhenzhi held the sovereign in his arms and issued orders by word of mouth—such loyal devotion in hardship is known to all.
value.literal: He also submitted a memorial arguing before the court, "At the time of Emperor Shizu's death, turmoil reigned within and without; Zhenzhi held the supreme sovereign in his arms and issued orders by word of mouth—such loyal devotion in hardship is known to all.

value.zh: 今希千戶侯，於分非過。」
value.en: To hope now for a marquisate of a thousand households would not exceed my due."
value.literal: To hope now for a marquisate of a thousand households would not exceed my due."

value.zh: 乃許三百戶。
value.en: Thereupon he was granted three hundred households.
value.literal: Thereupon he was granted three hundred households.

value.zh: 瞋恚形於言色，進為五百戶，又不肯受。
value.en: Anger showed in his speech and countenance. The grant was raised to five hundred households, yet he still refused to accept.
value.literal: Anger showed in his speech and countenance; the grant was raised to five hundred households, yet he still refused to accept.

value.zh: 明帝議誅之，乃許封汝南縣。
value.en: When Emperor Ming deliberated on executing him, the court finally granted him enfeoffment as count of Runan county.
value.literal: When Emperor Ming deliberated on executing him, he finally granted enfeoffment as Count of Runan county.

value.zh: 明帝即位，高、武舊人鮮有存者，法亮以主署文事，故不見疑，位任如故。
value.en: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, few of the old associates of Gao and Wu survived. Faliang, because he chiefly handled documentary affairs, was not suspected and retained his post and duties as before.
value.literal: When Emperor Ming ascended the throne, few of the old associates of Gao and Wu survived; Faliang, because he chiefly handled documentary affairs, was not suspected and retained his post and duties as before.

value.zh: 先是延昌殿為武帝陰室，藏諸服御，二少帝並居西殿。
value.en: Earlier, Yanchang Hall had served as Emperor Wu's private chamber, storing his robes and accoutrements. The two young emperors both resided in the West Hall.
value.literal: Earlier, Yanchang Hall had served as Emperor Wu's private chamber, storing his robes and accoutrements; the two young emperors both resided in the West Hall.

value.zh: 及明帝居東齋，開陰室，出武帝白紗帽、防身刀，法亮歔欷流涕。
value.en: When Emperor Ming took up residence in the Eastern Fast Hall and opened the private chamber, bringing out Emperor Wu's white gauze cap and personal dagger, Faliang sobbed and wept.
value.literal: When Emperor Ming took up residence in the Eastern Fast Hall and opened the private chamber, bringing out Emperor Wu's white gauze cap and personal dagger, Faliang sobbed and wept.

value.zh: 永泰元年，王敬則事平，法亮復受敕宣慰諸郡，無所納受。
value.en: In the first year of Yongtai, after Wang Jingze's revolt was settled, Faliang again received orders to proclaim comfort to the various commanderies and accepted no gifts.
value.literal: In the first year of Yongtai, after Wang Jingze's revolt was settled, Faliang again received orders to proclaim comfort to the various commanderies and accepted no gifts.

value.zh: 東昏即位，出法亮為大司農。
value.en: When Emperor Donghun ascended the throne, Faliang was transferred out as minister of grand agriculture.
value.literal: When Emperor Donghun ascended the throne, Faliang was transferred out as Minister of Grand Agriculture.

value.zh: 中書權利之職，法亮不樂去，固辭不受。
value.en: The Secretariat was the post of power and profit. Faliang was unwilling to leave and firmly declined, refusing to accept.
value.literal: The Secretariat was the post of power and profit; Faliang was unwilling to leave and firmly declined, refusing to accept.

value.zh: 既而代人已到，法亮垂涕而出，卒官。
value.en: Before long his replacement arrived. Faliang wept as he departed and died in office.
value.literal: Before long his replacement arrived; Faliang wept as he departed and died in office.

value.zh: 范仲淹
value.en: Fan Zhongyan
value.literal: Fan Zhongyan

value.zh: 蘇轍論殿試策問，引漢昭變武帝法度事。
value.en: Su Zhe, in discussing the palace examination questions, cited Emperor Zhao of Han changing the institutions of Emperor Wu.
value.literal: Su Zhe, discussing palace examination questions, cited Emperor Zhao of Han changing Emperor Wu's institutions.

value.zh: 哲宗震怒曰：「安得以漢武比先帝？」
value.en: Emperor Zhezong erupted in anger: "How dare you compare Emperor Wu to the late emperor?"
value.literal: Zhezong erupted: "How dare you compare Emperor Wu to the late emperor?"

value.zh: 轍下殿待罪，眾不敢仰視。
value.en: Su Zhe left the hall to await punishment; no one dared raise his eyes.
value.literal: Zhe left the hall awaiting punishment; none dared look up.

value.zh: 純仁從容言：「武帝雄才大略，史無貶辭。
value.en: Chunren said calmly, "Emperor Wu was heroic in talent and grand in design—the histories carry no word of blame against him.
value.literal: Chunren said calmly: "Emperor Wu was heroic in talent and grand in design—the histories carry no word of blame.

value.zh: 轍以比先帝，非謗也。
value.en: Su Zhe's comparison with the late emperor is not slander.
value.literal: Zhe's comparison with the late emperor is not slander.

value.zh: 陛下親事之始，進退大臣，不當如訶叱奴僕。」
value.en: At the beginning of Your Majesty's personal rule, advancing or dismissing great ministers should not be like scolding servants."
value.literal: At the start of Your Majesty's personal governance, advancing or dismissing great ministers should not be like scolding servants."

value.zh: 右丞鄧潤甫越次曰：「先帝法度，為司馬光、蘇轍壞盡。」
value.en: Right Vice Director Deng Runfu interrupted out of turn, "The late emperor's institutions were ruined entirely by Sima Guang and Su Zhe."
value.literal: Right Vice Director Deng Runfu interrupted: "The late emperor's institutions were ruined entirely by Sima Guang and Su Zhe."

value.zh: 純仁曰：「不然，法本無弊，弊則當改。」
value.en: Chunren said, "Not so—law by nature has no flaw; when a law proves flawed, it should be changed."
value.literal: Chunren said: "Not so—law by nature has no flaw; when flawed, it should be changed."

value.zh: 哲宗曰：「人謂秦皇、漢武。」
value.en: Emperor Zhezong said, "People speak of the First Emperor of Qin and Emperor Wu of Han."
value.literal: Zhezong said: "People speak of Qin Shihuang and Han Wudi."

value.zh: 純仁曰：「轍所論，事與時也，非人也。」
value.en: Chunren said, "What Su Zhe discussed was the matter and its time—not the man himself."
value.literal: Chunren said: "What Zhe discussed was the matter and its time—not the man."

value.zh: 哲宗為之少霽。
value.en: Emperor Zhezong's anger eased somewhat.
value.literal: Zhezong's anger eased somewhat.

value.zh: 轍平日與純仁多異，至是乃服謝純仁曰：「公佛地位中人也。」
value.en: Su Zhe had often differed from Chunren, but now submitted and thanked him, saying, "Sir, you are a man midway to Buddhahood."
value.literal: Zhe had often differed from Chunren, but now submitted and thanked him: "Sir, you are a man midway to Buddhahood."

value.zh: 轍竟落職知汝州。
value.en: Su Zhe was ultimately stripped of office and made prefect of Ru Prefecture.
value.literal: Zhe was ultimately stripped of office and made prefect of Ru Prefecture.

value.zh: 志第三 曆下
value.en: Treatise 3: Calendar, Part 2.
value.literal: Treatise 3, Calendar (Part 2).

value.zh: 改易者，其一，以舊法一章十九歲有七閏，閏數為多，經二百年，輒差一日。
value.en: First change: the old rule of seven intercalations in nineteen years inserts too many leap months; in two centuries it slips a full day.
value.literal: Of the changes—first, the old method had seven intercalations in nineteen years, the intercalation count being too many; over two hundred years it would shift by one day.

value.zh: 節閏既移，則應改法，曆紀屢遷，實由此條。
value.en: Once seasons and intercalation drift, the calendar must be revised—and that, I argue, is why systems have been rewritten again and again.
value.literal: Once the qi and intercalation shift, the method ought to be changed; calendars have been repeatedly altered—truly from this cause.

value.zh: 今改章法，三百九十一年有一百四十四閏。
value.en: My new intercalation rule yields 144 leap months in 391 years.
value.literal: Now changing the intercalation rule: in three hundred ninety-one years there are one hundred forty-four intercalations.

value.zh: 令卻合周、漢，則將來永用，無複差動。
value.en: Aligned with Zhou and Han practice, it should serve indefinitely without further drift.
value.literal: Making it accord with Zhou and Han, then in future use forever, without further deviation.

value.zh: 其二，以《堯典》雲：「日短星昴，以正仲冬。」
value.en: Second: the Canon of Yao says, "The days are short and the star is Mao—thereby fix mid-winter."
value.literal: Second, the 《Canon of Yao》 says: "The days are short and the star is Mao; thereby fix mid-winter."

value.zh: 以此推之，唐代冬至，日在今宿之左五十許度。
value.en: From that line, at the Tang dynasty midwinter the sun stood some fifty degrees west of its present lodge.
value.literal: Inferring from this, at the Tang era midwinter the sun was at about fifty degrees to the left of today's lodge.

value.zh: 漢代之初，即用秦曆，冬至日在牽牛六度。
value.en: At the Han founding the Qin calendar placed midwinter at 6° in Ox.
value.literal: At the beginning of Han they immediately used the Qin calendar; midwinter sun was at Ox six degrees.

value.zh: 漢武改立《太初曆》，冬至日在牛初。
value.en: Emperor Wu's Taichu Calendar moved it to the start of Ox.
value.literal: Emperor Wu established the 《Taichu Calendar》; midwinter sun at the head of Ox.

value.zh: 後漢《四分法》，冬至日在鬥二十二。
value.en: The Later Han Quarter-Remainder system put it at Dipper 22.
value.literal: Later Han Four Elements method: midwinter sun at Dipper twenty-two.

value.zh: 晉時薑岌以月蝕檢日，知冬至在鬥十七。
value.en: In Jin, Jiang Ji checked eclipses and found midwinter at Dipper 17.
value.literal: In Jin times Jiang Ji used lunar eclipses to check the sun, knowing midwinter was at Dipper seventeen.

value.zh: 今參以中星，課以蝕望，冬至之日，在鬥十一。
value.en: Comparing culminating stars with eclipse and full-moon tests, midwinter now falls at Dipper 11.
value.literal: Now comparing with culminating stars and testing by eclipses and full moons, on midwinter day the sun is at Dipper eleven.

value.zh: 通而計之，未盈百載，所差二度。
value.en: Taken together, the shift is two degrees in less than a century.
value.literal: Comprehensively reckoning, within not yet a full hundred years the discrepancy is two degrees.

value.zh: 舊法並令冬至日有定處，天數既差，則七曜宿度漸與曆舛。
value.en: Older systems pinned midwinter to a fixed longitude; as the sky moves, the seven luminaries steadily part from the calendar.
value.literal: The old methods all fixed the midwinter sun at a definite place; since the heavenly count has shifted, the seven luminaries' lodge degrees gradually diverge from the calendar.

value.zh: 乖謬既著，輒應改制，僅合一時，莫能通遠，遷革不已，又由此條。
value.en: Once the mismatch shows, reform is due; a fixed midwinter served one age but not the long term—and that too drove endless revisions.
value.literal: Once the error is evident, the system ought to be changed; it suited only one period and could not extend far—constant change also stems from this cause.

value.zh: 今令冬至所在，歲歲微差，卻檢漢注，並皆審密，將來久用，無煩屢改。
value.en: I would let midwinter advance slightly year by year; checked against Han observations it holds closely, and long use should not require repeated overhauls.
value.literal: Now making the midwinter position shift slightly each year, checking against Han annotations all are verified and precise; for long future use there will be no need for frequent changes.

value.zh: 韋世康，京兆杜陵人也，世為關右著姓。
value.en: Wei Shikang, of Duling in Jingzhao, came from a family that for generations had ranked among the notable surnames of the Guanzhong region.
value.literal: Wei Shikang—Wei Shikang was a native of Duling in Jingzhao; for generations his family had been a prominent clan of the Guanzhong west.

value.zh: 祖旭，魏南幽州刺史。
value.en: His grandfather Xu had served as inspector of Southern Youzhou under the Wei.
value.literal: His grandfather Xu was Southern Youzhou Inspector under the Wei.

value.zh: 父夐，隱居不仕，魏、週二代，十征不出，號為逍遙公。
value.en: His father Jiong had retired from public life; summoned ten times under both Wei and Zhou, he never accepted appointment and was known as the Duke of Leisure.
value.literal: His father Jiong lived in seclusion and did not take office; through the Wei and Zhou dynasties he was summoned ten times and did not emerge, and was styled the Carefree Duke.

value.zh: 世康幼而沉敏，有器度。
value.en: From childhood Shikang was thoughtful and quick-witted, with natural capacity and bearing.
value.literal: Shikang in youth was deep and keen, and had breadth of character.

value.zh: 年十歲，州辟主簿。
value.en: At the age of ten he was recruited by his province as chief clerk.
value.literal: At age ten he was summoned by the province as Registrar.

value.zh: 在魏，弱冠為直寢，封漢安縣公，尚周文帝女襄樂公主，授儀同三司。
value.en: While still young under the Northern Wei he entered the inner guard, was enfeoffed as Duke of Han'an, married Princess Xiangle, daughter of Zhou Emperor Wen, and received the rank of Pillar of State, Third Rank.
value.literal: Under Wei, at weak cap he became Direct Attendant, was enfeoffed as Duke of Han'an, married Princess Xiangle, daughter of Emperor Wen of Zhou, and was appointed Pillar of State, Third Rank.

value.zh: 後仕周，自典祠下大夫曆沔、硤二州刺史。
value.en: He later served the Zhou, advancing from lower grand master of sacrifices to governor in turn of Mian and Qia.
value.literal: Later he served Zhou, rising from Lower Grand Master of Sacrifices through the prefectures of Mian and Qia.

value.zh: 從武帝平齊，授司州總管長史。
value.en: When Emperor Wu conquered Qi, he was made chief administrator on the staff of the Si Province commissioner-general.
value.literal: Following Emperor Wu in the pacification of Qi, he was appointed Chief Administrator to the Commissioner-General of Si Province.

value.zh: 于時東夏初定，百姓未安，世康綏撫之，士民胥悅。
value.en: The east had only just been pacified and the populace was still unsettled; Shikang reassured them until officials and people alike were content.
value.literal: At that time the eastern regions had just been settled and the people were not yet at peace; Shikang soothed them, and gentry and commoners alike rejoiced.

value.zh: 歲餘，入為民部中大夫，進位上開府，轉司會中大夫。
value.en: A year later he was recalled to court as grand master of the ministry of the people, promoted to upper pillar of state, and then transferred to grand master of the department of accounts.
value.literal: After more than a year he entered the capital as Grand Master of the Ministry of the People, advanced to Upper Pillar of State, and transferred to Grand Master of the Department of Accounts.

value.zh: 協字欽仁，好學，有雅量。
value.en: Xie, styled Qinren, loved learning and possessed refined composure.
value.literal: Xie styled Qinren, loved learning, and had refined breadth.

value.zh: 起家著作佐郎，後轉秘書郎。
value.en: He began as assistant in the bureau of composition and later became secretariat gentleman.
value.literal: He began his career as Assistant in the Bureau of Composition and later transferred to Secretariat Gentleman.

value.zh: 開皇中，其父在廣州有功，上令協齎詔書勞問，未至而父卒。
value.en: During Kaihuang his father had distinguished himself at Guangzhou; the emperor sent Xie with a commendatory edict, but he arrived too late.
value.literal: In Kaihuang his father had merit at Guangzhou; the emperor ordered Xie to carry an edict of commendation, but before he arrived his father died.

value.zh: 上以其父身死王事，拜協柱國。
value.en: Because his father had died in imperial service, the emperor made Xie pillar of state.
value.literal: Because his father died in the king's service, the emperor appointed Xie Pillar of State.

value.zh: 後曆定、息、秦三州刺史，皆有能名，卒官。
value.en: He later governed Ding, Xi, and Qin in turn, earning a name for competence, and died in office.
value.literal: Later he served in succession as Prefect of Ding, Xi, and Qin—all had reputation for ability—and died in office.

value.zh: 洸弟藝藝字世文，少受業國子。
value.en: Guang's younger brother Yi, styled Shiwen, studied in his youth at the imperial academy.
value.literal: Guang's younger brother Yi—Yi styled Shiwen—in youth received instruction at the Imperial Academy.

value.zh: 周武帝時，數以軍功致位上儀同，賜爵修武縣侯，邑八百戶。
value.en: Under Zhou Emperor Wu he rose repeatedly through military merit to upper pillar of state and was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiuwu with eight hundred households.
value.literal: In the time of Emperor Wu of Zhou he repeatedly through military merit reached Upper Pillar of State, was enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiuwu with a fief of eight hundred households.

value.zh: 授左旅下大夫。
value.en: He was appointed lower grand master of the left brigade.
value.literal: He was appointed Lower Grand Master of the Left Brigade.

value.zh: 出為魏郡太守。
value.en: He was sent out as prefect of Wei.
value.literal: He went out as Prefect of Wei.

value.zh: 及高祖為丞相，尉迥險圖不軌，朝廷微知之，遣藝季父孝寬馳往代迥。
value.en: When Gaozu was chancellor, Yuwen Jiong plotted treason; the court had wind of it and sent Yi's uncle Xiaokuan posthaste to replace him.
value.literal: When Gaozu was Chancellor, Yuwen Jiong secretly plotted rebellion; the court slightly knew it and sent Yi's younger uncle Xiaokuan to gallop and replace Jiong.

value.zh: 孝寬將至鄴，因詐病，止傳舍，從迥求藥，以察其變。
value.en: As Xiaokuan neared Ye he feigned illness at a relay station and asked Jiong for medicine to probe his intentions.
value.literal: When Xiaokuan was about to reach Ye he feigned illness, stopped at the relay station, and asked Jiong for medicine to observe his changes.

value.zh: 迥遣藝迎孝寬。
value.en: Jiong sent Yi to welcome Xiaokuan.
value.literal: Jiong sent Yi to welcome Xiaokuan.

value.zh: 孝寬問迥所為，藝党於迥，不以實答。
value.en: Xiaokuan asked what Jiong was up to; Yi, loyal to Jiong, lied.
value.literal: Xiaokuan asked what Jiong was doing; Yi sided with Jiong and did not answer truthfully.

value.zh: 孝寬怒，將斬之，藝懼，乃言迥反狀。
value.en: Xiaokuan grew angry and was about to execute him; terrified, Yi revealed Jiong's rebellion.
value.literal: Xiaokuan was angry and was about to behead him; Yi feared and then spoke of Jiong's rebellious condition.

value.zh: 孝寬於是將藝西遁，每至亭驛，輒盡驅傳馬而去。
value.en: Xiaokuan then fled west with Yi, at every post driving off all relay horses.
value.literal: Xiaokuan thereupon took Yi and fled west; at every post station he would drive off all relay horses and leave.

value.zh: 複謂驛司曰：「蜀公將至，宜速具酒食。」
value.en: He also told each station master, "The Duke of Shu is coming—prepare food and drink at once."
value.literal: He again told the post official: "The Duke of Shu is about to arrive—you should quickly prepare food and drink."

value.zh: 迥尋遣騎追孝寬，追人至驛，輒逢盛饌，又無馬，遂遲留不進，孝寬與藝由是得免。
value.en: Jiong sent pursuers; at every station they found feasts but no horses and fell behind, so Xiaokuan and Yi escaped.
value.literal: Jiong soon sent horsemen to pursue Xiaokuan; when the pursuers reached the post they always met lavish feasts and again had no horses, so they delayed and did not advance—Xiaokuan and Yi thereby escaped.

value.zh: 高祖以孝寬故，弗問藝之罪，加授上開府，即從孝寬擊迥。
value.en: Out of regard for Xiaokuan, Gaozu did not punish Yi, promoted him to upper pillar of state, and sent him with Xiaokuan against Jiong.
value.literal: Gaozu because of Xiaokuan did not inquire into Yi's crime, added appointment as Upper Pillar of State, and immediately followed Xiaokuan in attacking Jiong.

value.zh: 及破尉惇，平相州，皆有力焉。
value.en: He played a major part in defeating Yuwen Dun and pacifying Xiangzhou.
value.literal: When they broke Yuwen Dun and pacified Xiangzhou, he had strength in both.

value.zh: 以功進位上大將軍，改封武威縣公，邑千戶。
value.en: For his achievements he was promoted to upper grand general and made Duke of Wuwei with a fief of one thousand households.
value.literal: For merit he advanced to Upper Grand General, changed enfeoffment to Duke of Wuwei with a fief of a thousand households.

value.zh: 以修武縣侯別封一子。
value.en: One son was separately enfeoffed as Marquis of Xiuwu.
value.literal: As Marquis of Xiuwu he enfeoffed one son separately.

value.zh: 高祖受禪，進封魏興郡公。
value.en: When Gaozu accepted the throne he was raised to Duke of Weixing.
value.literal: When Gaozu received the abdication he was advanced to Duke of Weixing.

value.zh: 歲餘，拜齊州刺史。
value.en: A year later he was appointed prefect of Qi.
value.literal: After more than a year he was appointed Prefect of Qi.
